News.title: Remains of baby girl found after being cut out of heavily pregnant mum’s womb as she was stabbed to death
News.content:
THE remains of a baby girl have been found after the unborn child was cut out of a heavily pregnant mum’s womb as she was stabbed to death.

María Camila Potosí, who was eight months pregnant, disappeared after leaving for a routine antenatal check on July 16.



The mum-to-be was found wrapped in sheets and buried beneath a pile of blankets on the banks of the Meléndez River in Cali City, Colombia, on 20 July.

When cops lifted the pile, they saw that her hands and feet were bound and her body bore multiple savage stab wounds, alongside clear signs she had been tortured.



María,21, had earlier helped care for a sick relative at her sister-in-law’s home in Meléndez before heading to her appointment.

She then sent her mum a quick message about a last-minute medical errand before disappearing.



Her husband raised the alarm when she failed to return home.

The horrifying discovery was made around four miles from her home.

Her unborn baby had been ripped from her womb and was missing.

María’s family were left desperately clinging to hope that the baby girl had somehow survived the brutal attack.



Her mum Alba Ruby Gómez said: “They told me the baby was not in her body.

“That filled me with hope she was alive.”

But police discovered the remains of an unborn girl in woodland near where María’s body was found yesterday, 30 July.

Investigators suspect the tiny remains belong to María’s daughter, who was due to be named Alahia.



Forensic experts must still carry out checks to confirm the baby’s identity, while preliminary findings suggest she died around the same time as her mum.

After the grim discovery, Alba said: “We weren’t expecting this.

“It hit us like a bucket of cold water.”

The heartbroken mum had previously pleaded for her missing granddaughter to be returned safely.



“The only thing I ask with this appeal and with the hopeful faith I hold that my baby is alive – is for her to be found,” she said.

“I ask that the people who have her search their hearts and return her to me.”

CCTV footage captured María’s final known movements on the afternoon she vanished.

She was seen climbing onto the back of a motorcycle ridden by a woman she had met two months earlier through a local support scheme for pregnant women.

Police have now arrested five people, including the woman who allegedly rode the bike.



She has been named as Yulieth Angulo, who investigators say built María’s trust over a number of weeks.

The rider reportedly gave changing accounts to investigators and remains a central focus of the chilling inquiry.

Cops suspect a gang plotted the kidnapping and murder, with one suspect allegedly coordinating the abduction while two others carried out the killing.

A fourth suspect allegedly dumped María’s body.

Two of the five suspects were already arranging passports to flee the country, according to police.



They face charges of aggravated femicide, kidnapping and forced disappearance.

One of the suspects allegedly gave police the exact location in the woods where the baby’s remains were found.

Before her disappearance, María had proudly revealed she was expecting a girl at a joyous gender-reveal gathering.



Surrounded by balloons and gifts, she was pictured beaming beside her husband as they celebrated the arrival of their baby.

The touching image was so precious to María that she made it her WhatsApp profile picture.

Relatives remembered her as kind, innocent and overly trusting, with her greatest dream being to become a mother and build a family home.

Cali Mayor Alejandro Eder said: “This is news I would not want to give.

“Today the baby of María Camila was found dead.



“This is a moment of pain for the family and the whole city.”

He demanded a strong punishment for those responsible.

President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella said the killers “do not deserve to be called human”.

He vowed tougher sentences so they never see freedom again.

Cali human rights ombudsman Gerardo Mendoza demanded a “swift, exhaustive investigation with a gender focus”.



He said the “extreme gravity” of the crime “cannot go unpunished”.

Meanwhile, senator-elect Jennifer Pedraza said: “They kidnapped, tortured and murdered a 21-year-old pregnant woman.

“In this country, nothing happens. We demand justice.”

Former presidential candidate Sondra Macollins said: “What impotence this causes. We trust that the Public Prosecutor’s Office and police will deliver rigorous answers.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The case is being investigated as a possible feminicide.



The investigation continues.

News.title: Callous funeral director who stacked up rotting bodies and gave grief-stricken families strangers’ ashes is jailed
News.content:
BEAST CAGED Callous funeral director who stacked up rotting bodies and gave grief-stricken families strangers’ ashes is jailed

A FUNERAL director who stockpiled dead bodies and gave their grief-stricken families ashes belonging to strangers was today jailed for 20 years.

Greedy Robert Bush, 48, raked in over £3.5million during an 11-year con which targeted hundreds of families at their most vulnerable.



He sold non-existent funeral packages, reused “scratched and dented” coffins and even trousered charity whip-rounds.

Profits were prioritised over people and relatives duped “on an almost industrial scale” so he could continue living the high-life.



After a five day sentencing hearing he finally learned his fate today as a judge said “I have very much in mind all those who have suffered in a variety of different ways from the defendant’s crimes.”

He continued: “Mr Bush took any and every opportunity through the course of his work to enrich himself… to the indignity of others.”

Sentencing Bush to a total of 20 years behind bars, Mr Justice Hilliard said: “I have no doubt that defendant behaved in such a deceitful way because of financial greed.

“He must unfortunately have a heartless side to him too which enabled him to treat the living and the dead in the way that he did.”



The judge added: “The defendant was so preoccupied with his own enrichment that he behaved in a shocking and disgraceful way to the deceased entrusted to his care and his behaviour to their living relatives was characterised by dishonesty, deception and heartlessness.

“If he could reuse a coffin paid for by someone else he would have done.”

Judge Hilliard KC said Bush’s offending was an “affront to public dignity” and a “gross breach of trust”.

Hull Crown Court was told how Bush discarded and abandoned bodies at his funeral home in the city and left them to rot whilst he lived the high-life.

During the scam Bush paid himself a whopping £162,000 a year and transferred a further £52,000 to his wife, Vicky, to keep more cash from the taxman.



He spent thousands on jewellery, enjoyed fine dining and blew a staggering £42,000 more on luxury holidays, flights and hotels.

Bush also splashed £21,000 on motorcycle racing and £17,400 on home improvements.

He spent a further £95,000 between 2017 to 2024 on areas described by the judge as “non-essential spending”.



The fraud “was not spontaneous or reactive” but “a deliberate commercial enterprise” to satsify his own levels of greed.

Christina George’s brother Raymond Dagnall, 64, was among the bodies discovered by police during a raid in March 2024. He had been there for a staggering nine months.

Speaking through tears she bravely told the court: “Bush would continually use the phrase ‘bless you’.

“These words used to sound endearing, peaceful and comforting.

“Now they just make me feel sick and the hairs prickle on the back of my neck.”



Sandra Samper, whose sister Maureen Graham, 82, was also among the bodies recovered, said: “She wasn’t just a body, she was a loved family member.”

Karen King, whose dad Norman Bridger, 94, was stored the longest, said: “My lovely dad lay in a cardboard coffin for almost 11 months.

“How could someone be so cruel? It is beyond belief.”

Jayne Rimmington, whose mum Shirley Wright, 86, lay undiscovered for five months, said: “It’s a purely evil thing to do.”

The family of Colin Wainman, 69, who was recovered from Legacy six months after his death, were given ashes in a cardboard box inside a Hobbycraft plastic bag.



His daughter, Vikki Mitchell, wept: “I don’t know how he slept at night knowing what he was doing.”

His vile scam was eventually exposed by chance whilst he was sunning himself on a luxury holiday in Arizona, US.

He asked another funeral director and his colleague to help one of his staff move a body from a care home.

They agreed but were left stunned when his employee suddenly confessed: “You two don’t know the half of it. Bodies have been there for years.”

The casual worker described the inside as “a horror scene” with cooling units switched off to cut costs and the smell unbearable.



The men accompanied him to the premises to investigate and later flagged down a passing police car to raise the alarm.

Cops ventured inside and found a large number of bodies – including the remains of four unborn babies – on racks inside a cold storage area.

Prosecutor Chris Paxton KC said: “The vast majority were uncovered and in varying states of decomposition.



“There was a further naked body lying on a stretcher on the floor.

“In addition, there was one sealed wooden coffin and four sealed cardboard coffins.

“Many of the bodies had hospital identity bracelets on their wrists and/or ankles, some had biological hazard bracelets, while others had no identifying markers.

“The area was dirty and unkept. There were a number of items on the floor which appeared to have been dropped or swept to the back.

“These items included flowers, rings, teddies, and cards with messages.



“These items were clearly personal possessions that loved ones would have wanted to stay with their deceased family members.”

Bush was arrested by cops at Heathrow Airport shortly after landing back in the UK from a holiday in the US with his daughter, Saskya.

He told them: “I f***ed it all up, everything, my whole world.”

In interview, police asked him if he had anything to say to the families affected. He replied: “No comment.”

His barrister, Richard Wright KC, said: “He has expressed himself to the court, and through the court to the families, as being sorry.



“Nothing I can say is intended to dull the families’ pain, anger or the sense of betrayal.

“The world has listened quietly as victim after victim after victim of Robert Bush has either come forward to read their own victim personal statements or has had their statements read on their behalf.

“He has heard witness after witness castigate his character and heard their entirely understandable anger, pain and outrage, all directed at him.

“And, all rightly directed at him.

“Dignity in death matters and there can be no hiding from the fact that, by his conduct, Robert Bush has deprived the dead and their families, of that basic dignity.”



Mr Wright said Bush had written to the court to apologise – adding: “He offers that apology without qualification and he accepts that responsibility.”

Mr Paxton KC said: “He was entrusted by hundreds of bereaved families, in their time of need, to treat their loved ones with dignity.

“Yet Mr Bush breached that trust on an almost industrial scale in a myriad of ways.

“The financial situation within the business was not dire, but likely mismanaged.

“The expenditure reflected Mr Bush’s priorities and not those whom he was meant to be serving.



“Mr Bush chose not to deal with those bodies entrusted to him but to operate as he chose and spend the money on himself and others.”

At sentencing today the judge told how the conditions inside Legacy were filthy, with clothes intended to be worn by his victims during cremation strewn across the floor.

He added: “There was a large quantity of family photographs that had evidently not been placed in coffins as intended.

“I have no doubt there was plenty of money to run or repair units if only he had chosen to run it that way.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Husbands and wives, partners, children, grandchildren now discovered they are left with nothing or in some cases we heard an empty plastic bag or a teaspoon of ash the police managed to recover for them.”



Bush previously admitted 30 counts of preventing the lawful and decent burial of a body, fraud by false representation and theft of up to £13,500 donated to 12 charities, including The Salvation Army and Macmillan Cancer Support.

News.title: Russian OnlyFans model, 21, fined £45,000 & banned from using internet after phone seized in Putin’s porn crackdown
News.content:
A RUSSIAN OnlyFans star has dodged prison but has been fined £45,000 and handed three-year internet ban amid Putin’s war on porn.

Sofya Vershinina, 21, has been convicted of producing and distributing explicit online videos in a Moscow court.



As part of her sentence she has been ordered to pay £45,000.

She has also been barred from appearing online, using the internet or from running her digital business for three years in a massive blow to her income.



Sofya, also known as Sonya Marmeladova, became one of many models charged by the Kremlin after President Vladimir Putin installed a nationwide crackdown on the state’s booming porn industry.

Russian prosecutors say she earned £300,000 from selling X-rated videos and sold intimate content on Telegram messenger while living in an elite Moscow skyscraper penthouse.



After pleading guilty and expressing remorse, she received a three-year suspended jail sentence that could take effect if she breaches the strict conditions.

She arrived at the Moscow court in a white Mercedes expecting a custodial sentence after prosecutors demanded three-and-a-half years in a penal colony.



Her gold iPhone 16 Pro Max remains seized but her sex toys and accessories that had been evidence in the case were returned.

Sofya is one of a number of high-profile models targeted by Russian law enforcement under the Putin crackdown on anti-traditional values.

Another model and influencer Diana Shurygina, 27, is currently custody awaiting trial.



Sources say the case against her centres on “intimate content” she allegedly sold to paying subscribers on OnlyFans.

Diana became a household name at just 17 when she appeared on television to reveal she had been the victim of a gang rape the previous year.

The explosive case led to the jailing of one of the men she accused and gripped the nation.



Anastasia Ovsyannikova, 24, known under the stage name Nastya Kholod, was also held on suspicion of illegal production and circulation of pornographic materials.

She and Diana made adult content for OnlyFans together and separately.

Alleged German producer of X-rated videos Ludwig Krichker was also detained and his residence was searched with equipment seized.

The Moscow Times reported earlier: “Criminal cases have started being launched in Russia for porn on OnlyFans.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Reports say state investigators in Putin’s Russia “have taken on the porn industry”.



Legal experts warn the net could widen even further on Putin’s enforcement on so-called “traditional values”.

News.title: Heart-stopping moment tourist freezes as bear sinks teeth into his leg before fleeing in terror after the beast pounces
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a tourist freezes as a wild brown bear bites his calf and lunges before the man flees in fear.

Bizarre footage shows the man standing stone-still when a bear creeps out of the bushes behind slowly in the Romanian Mountains.



The bear appears to sniff his leg tentatively for a few moments before taking a bite. The man remained still.

The dash-cam video shows the driver in the car driving forward slowly to box in the bear with the vehicle in front.



However, the bear remained unfazed.

The man can be seen leaning on the car bonnet before the beast suddenly strikes. The video captures the man fleeing in terror as his hands flail in the air, back to his own white car parked in front.

The video has gone viral on social media, racking up several million views.



Some users have commended his composure with the bear, arguing that staying frozen was the best choice as to not provoke the bear into aggression.

One said that “if he ran the bear would have run after him and potentially attacked him. Smart move.”

Others have been more bearish, saying that the man possessed “survival instincts of a potato”, and that “the fact that the bear waited for him to run, shows he is in it for the sport of it all”.

Tourists have previously been warned if they ever travel to the famous road Transfăgărășan, “do NOT STOP, DO NOT FEED THEM, and just AVOID THEM.”

The warning added: “No matter how chill and cute they might seem on the side of the road, almost ‘begging’ for attention and food, they are WILD animals and can be very dangerous, even deadly as you’ll soon find out.”



It comes after a bear killed a motorcyclist in the scenic mountain highway just a few days before.

The victim stopped at the popular tourist attraction with his bike despite there being a warning sign to not feed the bears.

A bear attacked him and dragged him down a steep ravine.

Romanian authorities have urged tourists driving along these highways to not approach or feed the bears.

Last year it has been reported that Romania may have as many as 13,000 brown bears, a protected species in the European Union.



And according to the government numbers of the past twenty years, brown bears have killed 26 people and injured 274 others.

Politicians have said that their growing numbers make attacks on humans more likely, and have doubled the authorised cull of brown bears to 481.

News.title: Convoy of THIRTEEN supercars worth over £2.5m seized after driving ‘at excessive speed & undertaking’ on UK motorway
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SUPER SEIZED Convoy of THIRTEEN supercars worth over £2.5m seized after driving ‘at excessive speed & undertaking’ on UK motorway

THIRTEEN supercars have been seized by cops after a convoy was spotted driving dangerously on a major UK motorway.

The high performance motors included Lamborghinis, a Ferrari, and a Porsche were all impounded on Tuesday.



Each driver was slapped with a warning for anti- social driving after motorists reported the drivers for a string of dangerous manoeuvres.

Witnesses told officers the supercars accelerated to excessive speeds before suddenly braking, bunching together and disrupting traffic.



The convoy joined the M11 from London just as rush hour was kicking off at around 4.20PM on Tuesday.

Drivers even allegedly used the hard shoulder to undertake other motorists.

Sergeant Will Willsher said: “The behaviour reported to us was not only anti-social but potentially placed other road users at serious risk, especially on a busy motorway during peak travel times.

“Roads Policing Unit officers acted quickly to locate the cars and take appropriate enforcement action.



“Speed limits are there to keep everyone safe and the law applies equally to all road users.”

Essex Police are appealing for witnesses who saw the convoy.

Anyone with information, dashcam footage or video recordings is asked to contact Essex Police quoting incident 955 of July 28.

News.title: Urgent hunt for man, 51, with ‘contagious condition’ after he suddenly disappeared from hospital as cops urge ‘call 999’
News.content:
AN URGENT search has been launched for a man who “may have a contagious condition” after he disappeared from a hospital.

CCTV released by Lancashire Police shows Dean Hesketh leaving Royal Preston Hospital at 11.16am on Tuesday (July 28) wearing a face mask.



Officers say they are increasingly concerned for the 51-year-old’s safety and welfare.

Dean, who also goes by Tim and Anthony Gledhill, has strong links to Preston, Penwortham and Blackpool.



He is described as slim, 5ft 4in with black hair and blue eyes.

He was wearing a khaki green and black jacket, a Lyle and Scott jumper, black trainers, and a blue surgical face mask.



Members of the public are warned not to approach Dean if they spot him as cops believe he could have a contagious condition.

A spokesperson for the force said: “If you do see Dean it’s really important that you get in touch with us on 999 as soon as you can, so that we can make sure he is safe.”

News.title: Migrant camps ‘growing more violent’ with guns seized as Border Force slam French cops for failing to stop small boats
News.content:
GUNS are being seized from French migrant camps as the criminal gangs behind them become increasingly violent, the Border Force said.

Officials are also said to be increasingly frustrated with hapless officers on the other side of the Channel who are failing to stop small boat crossings.



Gormless French officers watched on as 752 migrants left their shores for the UK on Wednesday, the busiest day for crossings so far this year.

It was later confirmed that four people had died off the French coast while undertaking the perilous journey.



The Gendarmes have long been criticised for failing to stop overloaded dinghies leaving, despite getting more than £1billion from UK taxpayers.

And in a concerning development, Border Force officials have now warned a “regular drumbeat of firearms” are being discovered in migrant camps.

A source told The Times: “They’re used to facilitate the smugglers’ activities — controlling patches, making sure they keep the spaces where they launch the dinghies and for enforcing protection

“The gangs controlling the crossings are involved in proper criminality.”



The Sun witnessed chaos unfold as asylum seekers repeatedly stormed beaches and fought each other for spaces on the small boats this week.

But as chaos unfolded, bungling French cops watched on and said: “Our order is to let them go.”

He added: “We just have to say to them ‘don’t do that, it’s dangerous’.”

Tory Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp was also on the beach in Hardelot and posted videos of the chaos.

He said: “The most shocking thing was the complete inaction by the Gendarmes.



“They just stood there and watched the migrants launching. It was extraordinary.”

More than 13,007 migrants have crossed the Channel so far this year.

But the heatwave has triggered a stampede and poses a fresh challenge to Mr Burnham, who name-checked immigration as a top public priority.

It comes days after PM Andy Burnham said the Government’s plan to curb Channel crossings was “working”, but admitted there was “more to do”.

On numerous occasions last year, The Sun watched on as officers on the coast of France unsuccessfully prevented small boats from setting sail.



In June, they were spotted for the first time in waist-high water using riot shields and pepper spray to disperse the migrant groups.

The officers finally went into the sea, but the small boats were still left dangerously overcrowded after the officers retreated.

A month later, we saw officers arrive an hour after a group of migrants waved au revoir from a packed dinghy headed for the UK.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Around 50 young East African men wearing life jackets were crammed on to the inflatable, which set off near Dunkirk.

The migrant “taxi boat” was even able to bob along in near-perfect sea conditions while waiting to pick up any stragglers.

News.title: Inmates ‘eating like dogs’ & loos ‘bubbling with waste’ in searing heat…pals slam hellhole jail where Andrew Tate held
News.content:
DEMONIC screams fill a cold, dark cell crawling with vermin, as droplets of filthy water slowly drip from a broken tap and the toilet overflows with stinking waste.

This is just a snapshot into the reported state of toxic Andrew Tate’s Federal lockup, where the controversial influencer – detained on rape charges – claims he’s forced to drink dirty brown water from a shower while inmates mark him with a “target”, as aides now reveal to The Sun the full extent of what they claim are the jail’s “disgraceful” conditions.



Andrew, 39, and his brother Tristan, 38, made names for themselves at the forefront of a social media empire promoting radical masculinity and misogyny followed by millions.

Now, they are held in a Special Housing Unit (SHU) at Federal Detention Centre, a concrete tower packed with 1,478 men in downtown Miami, as they face a slew of fresh charges, including rape, human trafficking and indecent images of a child.

Men awaiting trial are housed in scorching hot cells plagued by the stench of urine and faeces, and in statements posted on X, Andrew describes his SHU as “punitive housing for people who murder their cellmates”.



He also claimed he was staying in “the worst possible conditions the US gov provides to terrorists and psychopaths”, before adding the inmate in the neighbouring cell was a “cannibal who screams throughout the night”.

His only water source, he complains, is a shower and a “brown and filthy faucet” which has left him suffering “persistent stomach problems”.

In another message on X, Andrew woefully claimed he had “no commissary. No visits. No contact with the outside world.”



“I am an innocent until proven guilty extradition detainee. I’m wanted by a foreign state. I am an American citizen. WHY AM I HERE?” he demanded.

The harsh conditions were previously described by detainees in immigration and customs enforcement custody.

Last year, a report said inmates were forced to kneel and eat “like dogs”, with their hands shackled and food on chairs in front of them.

Toilets bubbling over with waste, crumbling infrastructure and an extreme use of force were also alleged by inmates’ families.



And as downtown Miami faces extreme heat, climbing above 30C, detainees say they have been left without air conditioning.

The facility has been blighted by AC issues for years, according to a 2020 report.

Inmates say they strip to their underwear amid the sweltering conditions and sweat through their sheets at night.

Earlier this month the Federal Bureau of Prisons said the facility “experienced a problem” with one of its chillers that provides AC. The malfunction has since been rectified, it said.



Andrew and Tristan were arrested at a bare-knuckle boxing event in Miami, US, on July 18, after British authorities issued 38 new charges against the pair.

It brings the total number of charges levied against the brothers to an astonishing 59.

The pair will have to wait behind bars for at least two more weeks before they face a detention hearing on August 13.

The hearing will determine whether they will stay in jail or be released for what could become a months-long court battle over their extradition.



Their legal team have until August 5 to file a motion for the brothers to be released on bail.

The Tates – who have dual US and UK citizenship – have repeatedly denied all charges against them.

Their attorney, Joseph McBride, told The Sun: “The conditions Andrew and Tristan Tate are being held in are a disgrace.

“Small filthy cells. Cockroaches. Shower water to drink. No chair. Lights they cannot control. Food that makes Taco Bell look like a Michelin restaurant.”



Their beds are “too small for men who are 6ft 3in and 6ft 5in” he added.

And they have only been allowed “three days outside since the day they were locked up”.

As they fester away in grim cells, the Tates’ lawyer said the pair face harassment from other inmates.



“There is serious concern that a target has been placed on Andrew and Tristan’s back”, he said.

“When someone becomes one of the most recognisable and polarising figures in the world, security is not a theoretical issue, it’s a real consideration.”

Prosecutors in the UK said the latest charges come after cops investigated claims from an additional four victims.

As accused child-sex offenders, they will be marked up “to get stabbed, jumped” or “murdered”, McBride said.

“That’s how the jail economy works”, he added.



Speaking outside court on Monday the lawyer said: “When inmates walk by their cell they get called a word that starts with a ‘P’ that’s more appropriate to [Jeffrey] Epstein and not to them.”

The brothers regularly speak with McBride from behind a Plexiglass window in prison, before they are hauled back into solitary confinement.

He has described his clients as “political prisoners” and victims of a scheming plot by the British government.

“Love them or hate them, the presumption of innocence must stand, they have been convicted of precisely zero crimes and they deserve to have their safety protected and their legal rights respected, just like anyone else”, McBride said.

McBride said outside court this week that Andrew is not personally accessing social media.



Instead, he passes messages through permitted communications with his legal team, which then publishes them online.

The White House has said it will not intervene in the extradition process, despite both Andrew and Tristan being vocal Maga supporters.

Marco Rubio, the Secretary of State, told reporters last week: “There’s no role for us to play at this moment, or maybe ever.”



Rubio has the ability to deny extradition and overrule the judges decision.

It follows a long-running legal battle involving the Tates that has spanned the US, Britain and Romania.

The brothers are already charged with rape, bodily harm, human trafficking and controlling prostitution for gain relating to three other accusers in the UK between 2012 and 2015.

They moved to Romania in 2016 where they were arrested and charged in 2022 with offences including having sex with a minor, trafficking minors, money laundering and running an organised crime operation.

US President Donald Trump’s envoy, Richard Grenell, allegedly persuaded Romanian authorities to lift their travel ban while awaiting trial there.



Grenell has said he did not have a “substantive conversation” about the Tates’ travel ban but added that he supported them.

The Tates arrived in Florida in February last year. Both Andrew and Tristan deny all charges against them.

The Bureau of Prisons has denied claims of poor conditions at the Miami facility.

A spokesperson told The Sun that inmates generally have access to commissary services, recreation, phone calls, social visits and legal counsel.

The agency also disputes claims that water at the facility is unsafe, citing its annual water certification from Miami-Dade Water and Sewer.



“Currently, the drinking water at FDC Miami is certified safe to drink”, a spokesperson said.

“An inmate may be placed in SHU not only for disciplinary segregation but also for administrative detention, which is non-punitive”, they added.

The BOP stated that “retaliation of any kind is not tolerated in our agency”.

It added: “Allegations of employee misconduct are taken seriously and, consistent with national policy, are referred for investigation if warranted.

“Incidents of potential criminal activity or misconduct inside BOP facilities are thoroughly investigated for potential administrative discipline or criminal prosecution.



“The BOP remains committed to ensuring the safety of our employees, inmates, and the public.”

News.title: Robert Bush sentence - live: Hull Judge delivers verdict on horrific funeral home scandal
News.content:
Former Legacy funeral director Robert Bush gave bereaved families the wrong ashes and left bodies decomposing in what one relative described as 'the most horrendous horror story'

Former undertaker Robert Bush - who gave bereaved families the wrong ashes and left the bodies of 35 people, including a stillborn baby, decomposing - has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Bush, 48, from Otley, West Yorkshire, kept his head down and was constantly blinking, but there were no tears as he heard the sentencing remarks at Hull Crown Court.

Judge Mr Justice Hilliard told the sentencing hearing he has never "known offences affect so many people and so many people so deeply". As he told the court Bush had shown regret and that it seemed genuine, many of the victims' families shook their heads. One woman broke down in silent tears.

Bush was sentenced for 67 offences spanning 12 years and affecting hundreds of victims at his business, Legacy Independent Funeral Directors, in Hull. His victims included the mum of a stillborn baby boy who discovered that her child's remains had been left on a floor for two years.

You can follow live footage of the sentencing here.

News.title: UK wildfires live: Colchester and Dunwich Heath blazes rage as huge areas scorched
News.content:
'Issue of wildfires around country needs careful investigation'

Asked what she believes the government should be doing now, Ms Coffey said: "I think the Prime Minister was right to offer resources straight away. It was good to hear there was no messing about with regards to that and indeed we know that fire services have come from right across the country in order to help.

"Clearly this issue of wildfires around the country needs a careful investigation I think into is it that recent policies have started to make that more, obviously climate change is a factor, but let's see what we can do to install firebreaks proactively in the future recognising if we're going to have these very hot summers for a long time."

Ms Coffey added: "To some extent we were fortunate being by the coast. I think that's massively helped in terms of access to water there.

"I think with Essex and Suffolk Water, they did increase the reservoir by about 50 per cent further down the coast, but nevertheless if we can do more to get on with reserviors being available that will help not only to stop hosepipe bans, but also be ready sources of water to tackle issues like this.

"What's been nice to see on the TV is people who have opened up their homes and the spirit of the community I enjoyed being part of here in Westleton when I was first elected.

"It's great to see that in action in such a sad circumstance, but just shows how the community came together to help others."

News.title: Manchester election results LIVE: By-election set to go to second count as Labour 'confident'
News.content:
Reform council chief threatens to report café owner who gives free meals to hungry kids to police

A café owner who served up free meals to hungry children after food vouchers were removed has been told he will be reported to police by a Reform council leader.

Barry Ashley, who runs the Grumpy Cook in Hastings, stepped up after East Sussex County Council decided not to issue school holiday meal vouchers to struggling families over the summer. He has criticised the move, which he branded “shameless”, accusing the council of turning its back of children in poverty.

He has since been told by Andy Woolley, who heads the authority, that he will be reported to police along with Labour MP Helena Dollimore. Mr Woolley claims to have been personally attacked online and accused the pair of inciting hate and potential violence by naming him in their criticism.

The dispute follows the council's decision not to continue offering the vouchers, which are a lifeline to families. An appalled Mr Ashley responded by announcing he would offer free meals to children who need feeding at his not-for-profit cafe.

A number of local businesses have donated to help, and Mr Ashley told The Mirror he has been providing more than 70 free meals a day. Ms Dollimore has launched a petition calling for the vouchers to be reinstated, branding the council's actions "totally unacceptable" and accusing it of putting children at risk.

Mr Ashley said: "Hastings is one of the poorest towns in the country. And it is by every measure it's a deprived town. One in three of the children are living in poverty.

"And the vouchers, just to take those away without considering what they should be putting in place, without doing any risk assessment, without doing any impact assessment, it's beyond bizarre."

News.title: Huge £1.5m book deal pulled after debut author is suspected of using AI
News.content:
Huge £1.5m book deal pulled after debut author is suspected of using AI

The publishing world has been shaken after a multi-million-dollar debut crime novel was pulled from release following accusations that the author used generative artificial intelligence

View 2 Images An unknown author has had a multi-million dollar book deal retracted over suspected AI use (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

The publishing industry was rocked today by news that a debut novel bought for over £1.5million ($2million) was pulled after the use of artificial intelligence was suspected.

‌



The auction for the hotly anticipated crime novel saw fourteen publishers bid for the right to publish in America. It was due to be published in a two-book deal with Minotaur, an imprint of Macmillan’s St. Martin’s Press, with plans to publish it in 2028.

‌



The Bookseller reported that the book “received multiple six-figure offers following a competitive multi-way auction in the UK.” Although details about the author’s identity remain unknown, Deadline revealed that the unpublished debut is titled Call Me, I’ll Hide the Body.

‌



View 2 Images Artificial Intelligence use for authors is a growing concern (Image: Getty Images)

Judges pick 'dynamite' Booker Prize 2026 longlist spanning ages 28 to 81 READ MORE :

The author’s primary agent Marc Gerald at Europa Content and UK agent Sandy Hodgman at Hodgman Literary submitted the manuscript to publishers as part of the selling process in July. Gerald told The Bookseller: “The book was stunningly good, everyone fell in love with it." The agents, however, withdrew the novel after doubts arose.

Publishing insiders told Publishers Lunch that those who had read the manuscript alleged that the book contained “many of the hallmarks of AI, including negative parallelism, off-kilter metaphors, and a flat prose style.”

‌



The author, who remains anonymous, spoke to The Bookseller after the fall-out from the AI controversy. They said: "The story, characters, scenes, humour, structure and voice came from me, and I have time-stamped drafts, written notes and dated WhatsApp messages documenting the book’s development. I am also concerned that AI-detector scores are being treated as conclusive evidence.

“I tested passages from books published in 2012 and 2017, and the software classified them as 98 and 99% AI-generated, despite their predating the widespread availability of generative AI.

"Within six hours of the rumours, I lost US, UK, translation, and screen opportunities without being given a proper chance to explain my writing process.”

‌



This incident comes on the heels of a landmark controversy earlier this year when publisher Hachette cancelled the US release of Mia Ballard's horror novel Shy Girl over similar AI concerns, reported by the New York Times .

The book - which was set for a US debut after selling 1,800 copies in the UK - was also pulled from British shelves, marking what The New York Times identified as the first instance of a major publishing house pulling a commercial novel due to evidence of AI usage.

Ballard strongly denied using AI herself. She explained to The New York Times that an acquaintance hired to edit her original self-published draft had introduced the AI-generated material without her knowledge.

Article continues below

Devastated by the fallout, Ballard noted she is pursuing legal action over the incident, sharing that the situation has left her mental health "at an all-time low".

Love reading? Join Dr. Aimée Walsh and our community of fellow readers in the Mirror Book Club to dive deeper into the books everyone is talking about.

News.title: UK wildfires map shows areas most at risk from infernos as fire rages near nuclear plant
News.content:
UK wildfires map shows areas most at risk from infernos as fire rages near nuclear plant

Half of England is now in drought due to soaring temperatures and low rainfall, the Environment Agency has warned – and this map shows the areas most at risk of wildfires.

View 3 Images Large forest fire on Dunwich Heath (Image: Suffolk County Council)

A map shows areas most at risk from wildfires in the UK as the battle continues to put out a blaze near Britain’s biggest nuclear power station.

‌



Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service has said that they were in a “better position” although they warned that the blaze near Sizewell B, at Dunwich Heath, near Leiston, was still a “dynamic incident”.

‌



In an update, the service said "crews and officers remained at the incident overnight" and "maintained a watching brief during darkness".

‌



Devastating wildfires are becoming increasingly common amid the climate crisis and this year has been especially dry with a succession of heatwaves.

Suffolk fire live: Dunwich Heath blaze rages as scorched area could take 25 years to recover READ MORE :

A map using data from the Moorland Association shows the wildfire threat across the country, highlighting the areas most at risk.

It shows that the High Peak constituency in Derbyshire - where the major moorland fire at Tintwistle Moor raged - is the area at greatest risk. Fire crews were first called to Tintwistle Moor, near Glossop, on June 24, and a major incident was declared there on July 13.

‌



Calder Valley, which covers part of West Yorkshire, including Hebden Bridge, where the acclaimed drama Happy Valley was filmed, is the second-most at-risk area. Tiverton and Minehead, which straddle the Devon-Somerset border, are the third-most-at-risk area.

There is generally a greater risk of wildfires in the west of England and Wales as well as large parts of Scotland.

‌



This week, the Environment Agency declared that half of England was in drought due to soaring temperatures and very low rainfall. Water Minister Emma Hardy has now warned people to prepare for this “new normal” wrought by climate change, as rivers run low, millions are placed under hosepipe bans - and wildfire risk increases.

Firefighters have been battling intense blazes around the UK this summer, including at Dovestone in Greater Manchester, Tintwistle Moor in Derbyshire, and Cairngorms National Park in Scotland.

Meanwhile, in Europe, a national emergency was declared in Spain as several wildfires merged into a single, uncontrolled front, and homes were evacuated in France.

‌



Andrew Gilruth, CEO of the Moorland Association, blamed rewilding campaigns for filling Britain’s uplands with “highly flammable vegetation” which is “burning at an incredible rate”.

View 3 Images A photo shows scorched burnt-out heath land near Sizewell (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

He called on new Prime Minister Andy Burnham to take “immediate action to allow farmers and gamekeepers to reduce this dangerous overload of vegetation”.

‌



“If he does not act, nature will be destroyed and there will be tragedies for firefighters and people sleeping in their beds,” said Mr Gilruth. He added that excess vegetation from rewilding was “sucking the ground dry” and, combined with climate change, was “baking the plants”, resulting in a “tinderbox Britain in which nature is turning into ashes”.

However, Rebecca Wrigley, chief executive of Rewilding Britain, said that “blaming rewilding completely misses the point”, adding that “simply stripping vegetation off our uplands is no answer to the wildfire threat”.

She said: “Britain's growing wildfire risk is being driven by climate change and the degradation of the living systems on which we all depend, not by efforts to restore nature.

‌



View 3 Images Water dropped on the wildfire by a helicopter (Image: Suffolk County Council)

“As hotter, drier conditions increase wildfire risk, the focus should be on preventing fires from starting through better public awareness, ensuring fire and rescue services have the resources they need to respond quickly, and creating landscapes that are more resilient when fires do occur.

“Healthy peatlands and beaver wetlands can create living, moisture-rich shields against wildfire. By restoring a mosaic of native woodlands, heathlands and wetlands, we can turn our soils into natural sponges and create firebreaks that slow the spread of flames.”

Article continues below

The Moorland Association assessed the “hazard” in each area by considering factors that could increase the threat of fire, such as the amount of vegetation that could provide fuel, climate triggers such as likely weather conditions, and terrain features that could amplify the threat.

“Exposure” covers what could be in harm’s way, such as property and habitats, and also assesses how difficult it would be to evacuate in the worst-case scenario.

Finally, “vulnerability” measures the site's fragility or preparedness, taking into account the age of the housing and the proportion of elderly residents.

News.title: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle took children 'on secret Scottish getaway' during UK visit
News.content:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle took children 'on secret Scottish getaway' during UK visit

It has been claimed that Prince Harry and Meghan travelled to Scotland during their recent trip to the UK with their children Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet and visited a remote island

View 6 Images Prince Harry and Meghan recently visited the UK (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Prince Harry and Meghan took their children on a secret getaway to Scotland during their recent trip to the UK, it has been claimed.

‌



But rather than heading to the royal estate of Balmoral, it is reported that instead they travelled to a remote island owned by a wealthy hedge fund manager. The Sussexes are claimed to have visited Tanera Mor, the island said to have inspired the cult 1973 film The Wicker Man, which was bought by billionaire Ian Wace, the co-founder of hedge fund firm Marshall Wace.

‌



Mr Wace bought the almost-deserted 800-acre island in 2017 for £1.7million and has reportedly ploughed £100million of investment into it to transform it.

‌



Prince Harry could face paying millions out of own pocket after failed legal action READ MORE :

View 6 Images It is claimed the Sussexes visited Tanera Mor in the Scottish Highlands (Image: Daily Record)

Now, many of the buildings and the natural landscape have been restored, and the Taigh Mor Foundation now hosts around 500 guests a year who work in the likes of the Police and Armed Forces so they can enjoy what is described as the island’s “calm and restorative” atmosphere.

It is believed Mr Wace is a friend of Harry’s with he and his former model wife Saffron Aldridge joining the Duke and Duchess at a Cirque du Soleil performance at the Royal Albert Hall in 2019.

‌



According to the Daily Mail, Harry is previously thought to have visited the island, where guests can help restore buildings, fish for mackerel and work in the kitchens and gardens.

Spokespeople for both the Sussexes and for Mr Wace declined to comment to the Mirror.

View 6 Images Meghan appeared to share a photo of a scene north of the border (Image: Meghan/Instagram)

‌



News of the alleged visit comes just a week after Meghan shared a glimpse into the Sussex family trip to the UK earlier this month in a series of Instagram snaps.

She posted a series of photos to her 4.7million Instagram followers with the caption ‘Summer Holiday’, with the carousel of 12 pictures including one snap that appeared to have been taken in the Scottish Highlands, showing a large loch.

In addition, the pictures also revealed that she, Prince Harry and their children Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet visited Althorp - the Spencer family home, where the late Princess Diana is buried.

‌



In one picture, Lilibet, five, is seen walking through the home's famous tree-lined gardens, while Harry and seven-year-old Archie walk ahead carrying bouquets of flowers.

6 View 6 Images Meghan shared a photo of Harry, Archie and Lilibet visiting Althorp (Image: Meghan/Instagram) 6 View 6 Images Meghan shared 12 photos from the family's trip to Portugal and the UK (Image: Meghan/Instagram)

‌



Other photos posted by Meghan and set to the Cliff Richard tune ‘Summer Holiday’, show the Sussexes in swimwear spending time at the beach, as well as Harry throwing his daughter up in the air as they play in a swimming pool and enjoying time in Portugal, where they had been enjoying a holiday before heading to the UK.

It has previously been reported that the Sussexes have a holiday home on the country’s Atlantic coast, close to where Princess Eugenie and husband Jack Brooksbank spend some of their time.

And in one photo, Meghan appears to share an image of the front of fish restaurant, O Melidense, in Melidese - in the same Alentejo region of Portugal.

‌



View 6 Images Harry flips Lilibet as they play in a swimming pool (Image: Meghan/Instagram)

Meghan is also photographed on a sun lounger beside a pool and in the background are a man and woman who have a striking resemblance to Harry's uncle Charles and his new wife, Cat Jarman.

In another sweet snap, Archie is seen in the cockpit of a plane wearing a pilot's hat, while the three staff members surround him as he is shown the controls. None of the photographs shows Archie or Lilibet's faces - a move by Harry and Meghan to protect their children’s privacy.

‌



The string of pictures also did not contain any photos of the Sussexes' family reunion with the King and Queen at Highgrove two weeks ago.

Harry and Meghan took their children to see their grandfather at his country retreat for the first time in four years earlier this month after the Duke previously said his security arrangements in the UK made it too dangerous to bring his family to his home country.

Article continues below

The children had last seen their grandfather on their previous visit to the UK for the late Queen's Platinum Jubilee celebrations in 2022.

News.title: Royal Mail rules on sending money in UK and abroad
News.content:
Royal Mail rules on sending money in UK and abroad

There is a list of restricted items as well

View 3 Images It's important to get it right (Image: Alamy/PA)

While much of our lives are digital these days, there are some things that can't be sent via email or message.

‌



That's why the postal service is as important as ever. If you need to get a physical item to someone anywhere in the world, it's there to make it happen.

‌



If those items are monetary or valuable in some way, there are rules and advice from Royal Mail to make sure they get there safely. There are also some restrictions on what can be sent.

‌



Royal Mail rules on s

Royal Mail recommends using its Royal Mail Special Delivery Guaranteed serice to send valuables, money or jewellery in the post. It says that money should be securely packaged and not visible from the outside. Senders also shouldn't indicate anywhere that money is inside.

View 3 Images Make sure you know the restrictions (Image: PA Archive/PA Images)

It also says not to send coins in envelopes, as its machines could damage them. That, it says, can cause delays or a greater risk of them being lost.

‌



Royal Mail definition of valuables

Royal Mail has a list of what is deems to be valuable when it comes to post:

Precious metal that has been manufactured in such a way as to add value to it, including coins used for ornament

Ingots

Diamonds and precious stones

Watches the cases of which are made wholly or mainly of precious metal

Articles similar to the above with an intrinsic value

Coins & bank notes of any currency that are legal tender at the time of posting

Postal Orders, cheques and dividend warrants uncrossed and payable to bearer

Unused postage, revenue stamps, National Insurance stamps, exchequer bills, bills of exchange, promissory notes and credit notes, bonds, bond coupons and any other investment certificates

Coupons, vouchers, tickets, tokens, cards, stamps and other documents that can be exchanged in whole or in part for money, goods or services

Royal Mail rules on sending valuables, money and restricted items abroad

To send these items abroad, Royal Mail recommends using its International Tracked service. That ensures extra compensation cover, with the maximum for loss or damage to international mail conatining cash being £100.

‌



Again, Royal Mail recommends packaging money securely. It adds: "Take care to make sure it's not visible through the envelope. Don't indicate on the outside of the packaging that money is inside. Don’t send coins in envelopes. Our machines might damage them, causing delays and a higher risk of loss."

View 3 Images Royal Mail has rules for what you can and can't send (Image: PA Archive/PA Images)

Countries where money cannot be sent

Royal Mail adds that many countries don't allow money to be sent through their postal networks and clarifies that it can't accept liability for loss or damage to money sent to these destinations:
