News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibugyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibugyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibugyo species replaces Zaire.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino’s top aide’s damning statement in full after QUITTING over ‘irresponsible’ World Cup sale plot
Sports.content:
A SENIOR adviser to Fifa chief Gianni Infantino has released a damning statement after resigning in protest over their World Cup sell-off plan.

Former US Soccer president and Goldman Sachs vice-chair Carlos Cordeiro suddenly stepped down from his role as an aide to the controversial executive on Friday.



The move came in response to Fifa‘s proposal to create a subsidiary company called the Fifa Forward Enterprise, which would oversee the World Cup.

Private investors would then be able to purchase stakes in the company, essentially taking ownership of a chunk of the World Cup.



Cordeiro slammed the proposal as a “bad deal for football” and called a number of Fifa’s claims into question.

His statement read: “As a senior adviser to the FIFA president, a former banker, and a lifelong football fan, I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup.



“Let me be clear: I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally.

“It is a bad deal for FIFA’s Member Associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.

“Football has been central to my life, and after more than 35 years in banking, I understand both the value of this asset and the consequences of giving part of it away. That is why this proposal should be rejected.

“FIFA already has access to extraordinary financial resources. The organisation sits on billions of dollars in reserves and no debt.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“The FIFA President himself has highlighted the $15 billion in revenue generated between 2022 and 2026.

“If Member Associations believe additional investment is needed to develop the game, FIFA already has the financial capacity to provide that support from its existing resources.

“Against that backdrop, selling a permanent stake in football’s most valuable asset to raise $4.2bn makes little sense. It is mortgaging football’s future without any compelling justification.

“Such economic success was not accidental. It was delivered by experienced football professionals who shattered FIFA’s commercial records. Yet despite those achievements, FIFA is now being asked to believe that outside investors are needed to unlock greater value.



“I do not accept that proposition. The people who built this success have already demonstrated that FIFA possesses the expertise to continue growing both the game and its commercial future.”

Cordeiro joins a number of the game’s most powerful voices in slamming the plans.

Uefa have vowed that none of its member associations will compete in a Fifa tournament while the plans are going ahead, and released an explosive statement earlier this week condemning the cynical proposal.

Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation also slammed the plans while stopping short of Uefa’s boycott pledge.

Uefa's boycott statement in full UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors. The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale. It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football. National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a “democratic decision”, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game. But our opposition goes far beyond process. The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders. This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain. Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation. As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership. Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination. There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments. Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.

Fifa had just hours earlier affirmed their intentions to push forward with the controversial project in a statement.



They said: “We have heard the feedback provided by the respective confederations in relation to the proposed establishment of Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) and would like to address the issues that have surfaced since the initial media reporting on Tuesday.

“We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation.

“Nobody is selling football. This is not something Fifa would ever entertain.”

Sports.title: Infantino’s unlikely journey from being bullied in tiny village to befriending Putin and being football’s most hated man
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO vowed to clean up Fifa’s image and put “football at centre stage” when he was elected the game’s most powerful man in 2016.

A decade on, Infantino has also become world football’s most hated man following his outrageous plan to privatise the World Cup.



All Uefa nations, including England, have vowed to BOYCOTT the World Cup if Infantino’s controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise plan comes to fruition – essentially the launch of a sister company that would allow world football’s governing body to sell a chunk of its tournaments to private investors.

The North and Central American as well as the Asian football federations have since followed suit, issuing damning rejections of the proposals.



But Infantino has vowed to plough on with his greedy plot regardless, despite all the backlash.

Uefa, Infantino’s former employers of more than 15 years, have called his plans “irresponsible and indefensible”, with the feud between European football and Fifa’s current regime seemingly broken beyond repair.

Then-FA director David Gill hailed Infantino’s Fifa presidential election “a good day for football” in February 2016, while FA chairman of the time Greg Dyke called the Swiss chief “a straightforward guy”.

So how has it come to this?

Infantino’s story begins in the Swiss Alpine town of Brig, where he was born on March 23, 1970.

The youngest of three children, the future Fifa chief was born to working class Italian immigrant parents – his father Vincenzo worked on the region’s night train service and his mother Maria at the station kiosk.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Infantino grew up with flame red hair and a freckled face and was immediately a football addict.

His infamous 2022 speech, in which he uttered “Today I feel Qatari. Today I feel Arabic. Today I feel African. Today I feel gay. Today I feel disabled. Today I feel [like] a migrant worker,” had another less well remembered line.

“But I feel like them because I know what it means to be discriminated and bullied as a foreigner in a foreign country,” he went on to add.

Infantino then elaborated: “As a child, I was bullied – because I had red hair and freckles, plus I was Italian, so imagine.”



His cousin Daniel Nellen told The Athletic last year: “(From) The Swiss, we felt this racism. Gianni had red hair and his skin had freckles. This was not too much of a big problem. The problem more was (being) Italian.”

A boyhood Inter Milan fan, the young Infantino attempted to make his way in the game, but did not go beyond his local FC Brig-Glis’ third team, for whom his mother would wash the kits.

Having given up on his playing dreams, albeit not without first becoming Brig-Glis’ club president, Infantino headed to the University of Fribourg, around a two-hour drive west of his hometown, to study law.

Nellen added of his cousin: “He said, ‘If I’m not good enough (to be a footballer), I want to be the lawyer of the footballer’. Always, his idea was to make something with football.”

After graduating in the 1990s, Infantino went on to land a job with the International Centre for Sports Studies (CIES).



In his legal adviser role he helped develop the Fifa Master programme, a qualification in Management, Law and Humanities of Sport that still exists today.

Infantino’s work with the CIES saw him earn his first role at Uefa in August 2000, initially slotting into their legal department.

During those early days with Uefa, Infantino married Leena Al Ashqar in 2001, with the couple going on to have four daughters together.



A talented linguist, Infantino is said to speak seven languages, including Arabic, and was even handed Lebanese citizenship earlier this year.

After holding various roles within Uefa’s legal team, Infantino’s career really began to take off following Michel Platini’s 2007 election as president.

That same year, Infantino secured a new role as deputy general secretary, and in October 2009 he was promoted to Uefa’s General Secretary – one of the governing body’s most important positions beneath Platini.

In this public-facing position Infantino became synonymous to fans for his prominent role in conducting draws, most notably for the Champions League.

As Uefa general secretary Infantino played significant parts in the roll-out of Financial Fair Play between 2009 and 2011, as well as the 2014 Uefa Nations League launch and the build-up to the expanded Euro 2016.



Despite his ever-increasing profile, Infantino was not widely tipped to land the top job at Fifa during this period – in fact, it was his boss Platini touted for the role.

But then a huge scandal at the heart of Fifa and Uefa granted Infantino a huge opportunity.

Sepp Blatter was re-elected as Fifa president in 2015 only to announce his intention to resign amid a corruption scandal just days later.



Platini was a leading contender to replace Blatter, until it emerged that Swiss cops were investigating payments made between the two.

Both men were handed lengthy bans, although each has since been cleared of wrongdoing in court.

Infantino subsequently announced his candidacy, with a source recently telling The Telegraph of his campaign, compared to Platini’s: “He may not have copied and pasted it, but he might as well have done so.”

In February 2016, Infantino defeated AFC president Salman Ibrahim Al Khalifa to be elected Fifa president, ironically with the help of a €500,000 (£438,000) campaign donation from now-bitter enemies Uefa.

He said at the time: “I want to be the president of all of you. I travelled through the globe and I will continue to do this. I want to work with all of you to restore and rebuild a new era where we can put football in the centre of the stage.



“We enter now a new era. We’ll restore the image of Fifa and make sure everybody will be happy with what we do.”

In Infantino’s decade at the helm, Fifa, a non-profit organisation, has continued the aggressive commercialisation that had started under Blatter.

Infantino’s biggest legacies to date are the expanded 48-team World Cup in the United States, and the revamped 32-team Club World Cup that was staged in the US 12 months ago, much to the annoyance of many teams.



The 2034 World Cup was controversially awarded to Saudi Arabia despite huge concerns about its human rights record and another winter tournament, after the Middle Eastern nation ran unopposed.

Australia had been interested in a bid, but withdrew amid suggestions that such a campaign against the financial might of the Saudis would be futile.

In his role, Infantino rubbed shoulders with Vladimir Putin ahead of the 2018 World Cup in Russia, and the following year was awarded an Order of Friendship from the Kremlin leader.

He then befriended US president Donald Trump – the American calling him the “king of football” after being handed the farcical inaugural “Fifa Peace Prize” last December.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

As Infantino’s latest plan threatens to tear apart the fabric of the sport while waging war with his former employers, one former Uefa colleague told The Athletic: “I don’t recognise the Gianni I see and hear now.”



With Infantino’s future as head of Fifa now seemingly hanging by a thread, the most hated man in football may be forced to take on yet another new guise sooner than he likes.

Sports.title: England hero Chloe Kelly reveals goals for new WSL season – but says she is NOT looking to World Cup yet

CHLOE KELLY knows just how quickly football can change.

Mullins is best known for his time in the Premier League at West Ham where he played between 2003 and 2009.

The Magpies had been reluctant to part with their captain but Arsenal have gone all out to get the deal done.



And according to L’Equipe, the two sides have reached a broad agreement over a proposal worth £77million plus bonuses.

A few details, including agent’s fees, still need to be ironed out before the deal is considered done.



But the massive breakthrough should unlock the Brazilian’s move to North London, with personal terms on a five-year contract already agreed.

Guimaraes dropped a bombshell on the Newcastle hierarchy several weeks ago by informing them of his desire to leave.

And he did not fly with the rest of the Toon squad to their pre-season training camp in La Manga on Friday.

Newcastle hope to jet him out on Sunday for talks with incoming boss Matthias Jaissle after his extended post-World Cup break, but all the indications are that a deal could be sewn up by then.

The captain’s departure would cap off a woeful week on Tyneside, where fans are mourning the sudden departure of Eddie Howe.

The long-serving manager reportedly quit over transfer frustrations, and because he believed the club would sell Guimaraes, which was ‘the final straw‘.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

To add insult to injury, around £6.8m of the transfer fee will be paid to Lyon, who were granted 20 per cent of the profit from a Newcastle sale when they negotiated his £40m switch to St James’ Park in 2022.

Arsenal have already completed a handful of deals this summer, with Piero Hincapire joining permanently after his loan move from Bayer Leverkusen.

Illan Meslier has join from Leeds on a free transfer, with Christos Tzolis arriving from Club Brugge for £34m.

The Gunners are expected to sign another attacker before the end of the window, with Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez both targets.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal update, Man Utd Rashford call, final Vini Jr decision
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal star expresses concern about Chelsea's transfers

Paul Merson has admitted he is not completely convinced by Chelsea's moves for Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson. He said to Sky Sports: "I've always screamed out that Chelsea need experience. And those two players are experience. People are going to say: 'Oh, what are they buying 35-year-olds for?' It's not about the future for Chelsea, it's about the here and now.

"They've gone for the future before with players on seven, eight-year contracts. And if it was successful, they would have been the most successful team in the world for many a year, but it hasn't worked like that. So you need experience with these kids. They're buying good young players but you still need experience. It's priceless, experience.

"They're not going to play every game when it goes well. But when Chelsea do have games when it isn't going well and the crowd get a bit restless, that experience helps, believe me. I like Welbeck. I don't know him as a person, but he comes across as a lovely bloke and a good professional.

"If you look at his record the last two years at Brighton, it's been amazing. But he's played a lot of football - and he needs to play a lot of football when you're his age. If you look at his record, he played 30-odd games last year and then 30-odd games the year before. He's not going to get 30-odd games this year.

"It's hard to stop-start when you get to a certain age. You need to keep on playing. You can't keep on just playing a game here or there. It just isn't the same. I know what it's like. I played until I was well into my 30s. You had to play all the time. When you didn't play all the time, it got hard."

Sports.title: FIFA president Gianni Infantino was backed by The FA in statement that now looks laughable
Sports.content:
The FA fully backed Gianni Infantino's FIFA presidency bid back in 2016. The then-FA chairman, Greg Dyke, hailed him as a “straightforward guy” whilst ex-Manchester United chief David Gill maintained it was “a good day for football”.

Infantino triumphed over the former Asian Football Confederation president, Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa, by 115 votes to 88 and the FA were fully behind the former UEFA man landing the top job. A decade on and they're putting out statements condemning his grand plans to sell out stakes in the World Cup.

Dyke claimed at the time that Infantino's victory was a new start for FIFA. Gill had been one of Sir Alex Ferguson's key lieutenants at Manchester United but moved on to become the FA director who also sat on the executive committee at both UEFA and FIFA. He too was thrilled to see Infantino’s election.

Infantino vowed to "restore the image of FIFA and make sure everybody will be happy with what we do" when he was elected. A decade on from that opening statement and the former UEFA general secretary is now fighting for his job after his latest controversy.

‌



Infantino's spell as the man in charge of world football has been marred by moves seen in some quarters as little more than money grabbing, even if the Swiss-Italian once claimed that "it’s your money, not the money of the FIFA president".

When he was appointed as FIFA's president the organisation was at an extremely low ebb following a spell under Sepp Blatter marred by corruption. Infantino vowed to change that perception, but as the years have gone on his moves have appeared more and more self obsessed.

His latest move, a desire to sell stakes in FIFA's tournaments, the main one being the World Cup, to outside investors is seen purely as a financial coup.

‌



View 3 Images Former FA Chairman Greg Dyke was fully behind the election result ten years ago

None of the major federations around the world, led by UEFA, want anything to do with it and, given it would need member approval, it looks like the proposal is already dead in the water. UEFA branded the proposal "irresponsible and indefensible" while labelling Infantino's offer of £30m to FIFA's 211 members to endorse his new enterprise - while warning nations they wouldn't get that cash if it ultimately passed but they voted against him - as "governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game."

Even before this drastic World Cup plot, Infantino had been the man who presided over an expanded World Cup, which opened doors to lesser nations, but also helped raise more cash for FIFA given the additional games. The World Cup we've just seen was overshadowed by ludicrious ticket prices, which Infantino continued to defend.

He's also masterminded a new Club World Cup, which went from seven teams to 32. That again was seen by some as FIFA trying to create a rival to the Champions League, UEFA's tournament which remains the most revered club competition in the world. The expanded Club World Cup showed little regard for player welfare given the amount of games.

‌



All of which makes Infantino's desire to bring FIFA out of the doldrums all the more laughable 10 years on, with the former UEFA man's legacy looking increasingly tarnished.

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino said he would "restore the image of FIFA"

He claimed: “We enter now a new era. We’ll restore the image of FIFA and make sure everybody will be happy with what we do.”

Speaking to those who voted for him he vowed: “I want to be the president of all of you. I travelled through the globe and I will continue to do this. I want to work with all of you to restore and rebuild a new era where we can put football in the centre of the stage. Fifa has gone through sad times, moments of crisis. But those times are over.”

‌



Despite the factions that now exist, the FIFA president once hailed: “I’m a candidate of the whole world and football. We have to build bridges, not walls.”

The irony now being that the walls are firmly caving in with three federations issuing statements to combat his World Cup plans, some calling for change. All whilst Infantino loses those around him as the faith in him diminishes.

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand's son signs for Premier League club as Man Utd icon sends four-word message
Sports.content:
Rio Ferdinand's son signs for Premier League club as Man Utd icon sends four-word message

Rio Ferdinand was one of the greatest England defenders of all time and now Manchester United great's name looks set to live on in the Premier League

View 2 Images Another one of Rio Ferdinand's son has signed a pro contract with a Premier League club (Image: Lev Radin/Shutterstock)

The son of Manchester United legend Rio Ferdinand has signed a professional contract - with Brighton and Hove Albion. Tate Ferdinand, 17, has been playing with the Seagulls' U21s side, having first joined the club in 2024.

‌



He made a huge contribution to the South Coast team last season, playing a key role on their way to reaching the Sussex Transport Senior Cup final. Tate is not the first son of the former England captain to sign a pro deal at the Amex Stadium.

‌



Lorenz Ferdinand, who is a goalkeeper, also put pen to paper on a pro deal in Sussex, having spent some time on loan with non-league side Havant and Waterlooville in the past.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd transfer talks confirmed as agent says deal is close READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford posts Barcelona farewell message as dream return goes up in smoke READ MORE :

Over a fortnight since Lorenz committed his future to the club, Tate has followed suit to the delight of a beaming Ferdinand and his ex-team-mate Edwin van der Sar, who left a kind four-word message for the teen prodigy.

Confirming the news on Instagram, the ex-United central defender wrote: "Proud moment with the family, my boy Tate Ferdinand signing his first pro contract. Keep up the hard work.”

‌



Van der Sar was one of the first of Ferdinand’s United team-mates to say congratulations, commenting: “All the best Tate," while Darren Fletcher also wrote: "Love it" alongside some clapping emojis.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Last season, then Brighton U18s coach Bjorn Hamberg did his best to urge fans and other figures in football to not let the fact Tate is the son of Ferdinand put more pressure on his young shoulders.

‌



Hamberg said: "Tate Ferdinand is Tate Ferdinand and he needs to be play his game and have his pathway and career. For us as a team, for the under-18s as a captain, he is a big voice in our dressing room. He is obviously a leader in the back line and playing very well for the moment. I am really pleased for him as well.”

The fact Tate is playing against players who are four years his senior suggests he is progressing at a quick rate. Last season, he made 24 appearances with Brighton's U18s side and even contributed two goals. Considering the trajectory of their careers, it's not impossible that Lorenz and Tate may feature together on the same team, just like Ferdinand did with his brother Anton.

View 2 Images Lorenz Ferdinand is also at Brighton (Image: Dave Haines / SWNS)

‌



Interestingly, when speaking about their development in 2025, Ferdinand revealed his football prodigy sons often ignored his advice, preferring to listen to the views and opinions of their coaches. He said: "Even though I played, when I told them about football when they were 12, 13, 14 years old, they were like ‘What do you know?'

"They were listening to their football coach – who’d never played a league game in his life or been a professional – and coming in and saying 'But so-and-so said this dad’.”

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes pushes for Arsenal transfer with Newcastle agreement imminent
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes pushes for Arsenal transfer with Newcastle agreement imminent

Arsenal are hoping to finalise the terms of Bruno Guimaraes' transfer with Newcastle by the time the player is scheduled to fly back to Europe from Brazil on Sunday, though he was initially due to report back to his current club today but has delayed his travel as he awaits a breakthrough on his future

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes did not return to Newcastle today, as initially planned

Arsenal are working to close a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes in the coming days in a transfer expected to reach at least £80million, potentially up to £85m with add-ons.

‌



The Gunners have seen two proposals, tabled via intermediaries, rejected by their Premier League counterparts, who have persistently denied any club-to-club contact to date.

‌



Arsenal's most recent offer was understood to be a fixed fee of £70m plus around £5m in contingents, which Newcastle did not deem acceptable.

‌



The very first initial discussions were around a £55m package plus additional bonuses. It was not a verbal proposal as such but the Magpies understandably did not warm to those figures.

The numbers then gradually, rose, first to £65m, then £75m and the next offer is expected to close the deal.

Bruno Guimaraes given separate Newcastle plan as showdown transfer talks scheduled READ MORE :

Sources at St James' Park have intimated frustration about Arsenal's left-field strategy, however, there is now a growing expectation that a deal will be struck following the bombshell departure of boss Eddie Howe.

‌



Guimaraes had initially been scheduled to return to Newcastle on Friday, however, he will not be travelling with the squad to their warm-weather training camp in La Manga this afternoon.

It's understood he has instead remained in Brazil, specifically in Rio de Janeiro, where he has spent the past few days with his father Dick Gomez and members of his representation. He was pictured playing padel with his dad, among others, on Thursday.

On Wednesday evening following the 4-1 friendly defeat to Bristol City, now-departed boss Howe indicated he expected Guimaraes to be back with the team this Friday, as he had also previously stated on July 26.

‌



When asked if his skipper would be travelling to La Manga with the squad, he told reporters: "That's a good question. The details, I don't actually know but I see no reason why that wouldn't be the case."

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes is edging closer to joining Arsenal from Newcastle United (Image: (Photo by Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

It's believed there has been a shift over the past 48 hours, not least because Arsenal are drawing closer to striking a full agreement with Newcastle. A verbal agreement over a five-year contract at the Emirates, has already been reached and the ex-Lyon maestro feels at this stage of his career, this an opportunity too good to resist.

‌



As club captain, Guimaraes has been reluctant to publicly agitate for a transfer like Alexander Isak did last summer but he has, on several occasions including in the past few days, reaffirmed his desire to pursue a switch to the Premier League champions.

Any slim hope of keeping the midfielder is thought to have evaporated since Howe's exit was confirmed on Thursday morning.

Sources from Guimaraes' inner circle confirmed he had initially planned to be back in England today but now, the subsequent 'delay' - which has materialised to facilitate the transfer - will provide the two clubs a window to finally resolve matters.

‌



Newcastle have been focusing efforts on finalising the terms and legalities of new boss Matthias Jaissle's contract, which is still deemed their utmost priority.

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes is now not due to train with Newcastle in La Manga until Monday (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

In the past few days, Guimaraes hosted a 'leaving party' in Brazil, however, the family celebration which also included a guest appearance from singer Belo was to celebrate the end of his summer holidays - not an impending transfer. The party was staged with a view to being back in England today.

‌



The 28-year-old also attended Vasco da Gama's 1-1 draw with Mirassol on Sunday as he awaited developments on his future back in England.

Arsenal are now set to proceed with all the formal steps required to finalise a deal with Newcastle before his planned return to training on Monday.

While the Magpies insist Guimaraes has been granted extended leave due to his involvement in the World Cup with Brazil, his delayed return is directly linked to his future.

Article continues below

He is still expected to report back to Newcastle training on Monday, he is set to travel on Sunday, if a resolution hasn't been found, honouring his contract.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino ally quits as FIFA boss blasted over World Cup plans in angry statement
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino ally quits as FIFA boss blasted over World Cup plans in angry statement

Gianni Infantino has opened a Pandora's box in his attempts to alter FIFA and the World Cup forever in a controversial fashion

View 3 Images Things look set to get worse for Infantino (Image: PA)

Carlos Cordeiro, a senior advisor to Gianni Infantino, has resigned from FIFA in protest against the Swiss figurehead's plan to alter its landscape forever. Infantino's idea to form a $20billion commercial subsidiary called 'FIFA Forward Enterprises' which would then see 20-30 per-cent of it be sold to outside investors, has been met by stern opposition across football.

‌



In response, UEFA promised to boycott all FIFA competitions for as long as the idea is still breathing, while the Asian Football Federation and CONCACAF - the federation for North America, Central America and the Caribbean nations - have also publicly opposed the plan. FIFA released a new statement in the early hours of this morning stating "nobody is trying to sell football" but the level of opposition is only increasing.

‌



So much so that Cordeiro, who has been a key ally to Infantino, has handed in his resignation after becoming enraged by FIFA's plan. He confirmed his exit in a furious statement.

‌



He wrote: "As a Senior Advisor to the FIFA President, a former banker, and a lifelong football fan, I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup. Let me be clear: I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally. It is a bad deal for FIFA's Member Associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.

"Football has been central to my life, and after more than 35 years in banking, I understand both the value of this asset and the consequences of giving part of it away. That is why this proposal should be rejected. FIFA already has access to extraordinary financial resources.

Gianni Infantino facing imminent FIFA wipeout as UEFA could take nuclear option READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"The organisation sits on billions of dollars in reserves and no debt. The FIFA President himself has highlighted the $15 billion in revenue generated between 2022 and 2026. If Member Associations believe additional investment is needed to develop the game, FIFA already has the financial capacity to provide that support from its existing resources.

"Against that backdrop, selling a permanent stake in football's most valuable asset to raise $4.2 billion makes little sense. It is mortgaging football's future without any compelling justification. Such economic success was not accidental. It was delivered by experienced football professionals who shattered FIFA's commercial records.

View 3 Images Cordeiro has resigned from his position as senior advisor to FIFA president Gianni Infantino (Image: AP)

‌



"Yet despite those achievements, FIFA is now being asked to believe that outside investors are needed to unlock greater value. I do not accept that proposition. The people who built this success have already demonstrated that FIFA possesses the expertise to continue growing both the game and its commercial future.

"Most troubling of all is the absence of answers to fundamental questions. Why this deal? Why now? What oversight exists? Who benefits? Was there a competitive process? What governance will be in place? What will investors ultimately gain, and at what cost to football?

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino has been dealt another reality check (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

‌



"These questions remain largely unanswered, and yet Member Associations are being asked to make a decision of enormous consequence in barely 50 days or risk being left behind. That is not a responsible way to determine the future of the world's game.

"This proposal has become a defining question for FIFA's future. After careful consideration, I can no longer continue in my role as Senior Advisor to the FIFA President. I have therefore resigned with immediate effect. FIFA's responsibility is not to maximise commercial returns at any cost. It is to protect and strengthen football for future generations. When those principles come into conflict, football must come first.

"It has been the privilege of a lifetime to serve FIFA for more than five years and to work alongside dedicated, principled people who care deeply about the game. I hope they, too, will speak up, because decisions of this magnitude should be made in the interests of football, not those who stand to profit from it."

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes given separate Newcastle plan as showdown transfer talks scheduled
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes given separate Newcastle plan as showdown transfer talks scheduled

Bruno Guimaraes will not head out to La Manga for Newcastle's pre-season camp with the rest of the squad as the club prepare to sit down with him again to discuss his future

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes continues to be liked with a Newcastle exit (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

Newcastle are planning to welcome Bruno Guimaraes to their pre-season camp on Sunday - where he will hold talks with new boss Matthias Jaissle regarding his future.

‌



The Brazilian has been given an extended summer break given his involvement at the World Cup, but throughout that time he's been linked with a St James' Park exit as Arsenal circle for the midfielder, who has expressed a desire to leave.

‌



Newcastle have already seen Anthony Gordon leave for Barcelona and Sandro Tonali then followed him out of the club, joining Tottenham in a £100million deal. Losing Guimaraes would perhaps be the biggest blow given he is their captain and talisman.

‌



But the Chronicle reports that the Brazilian will not be with his team-mates as they jet off to La Manga on Friday for their pre-season camp.

Arsenal close in on £80m Bruno Guimaraes transfer in major breakthrough for Mikel Arteta READ MORE :

Ex-Newcastle owner Amanda Staveley in talks to buy West Ham stake READ MORE :

Newcastle sources claim that Guimaraes has been handed his own travel plans and his delay in returning is thought to be part of his post-World Cup fitness programme.

Newcastle sporting director Ross Wilson will travel to La Manga with the team ahead of Jaissle's expected arrival this weekend after Eddie Howe chose to step away, albeit his exit has yet to be formalised. The ex-Red Bull Salzburg boss will have to prove to his star midfielder that he can create a winning outfit given their season and notable exits.

‌



In Howe's final interview he gave no promises that Guimaraes would remain in Newcastle given the club have been willing to sanction high profile exits for large fees.

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes has been given an extended break following his World Cup involvement (Image: (Photo by Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

He said: "We’ve spoken numerous times. Assurances? I don’t think you can push too hard for those. I’ve said many times we want players who are committed, and Bruno has always been committed.

‌



"His training performances and his game performances have been outstanding, every time he’s worn the shirt, he’s played with the fans by his side. I’d love to see that continue."

Howe also admitted: "What will be, will be. We can’t control the forces that are at play here".

Sports.title: Newcastle have ideal opportunity to sign 236-goal World Cup striker after Eddie Howe exit
Sports.content:
Newcastle have ideal opportunity to sign 236-goal World Cup striker after Eddie Howe exit

Newcastle United could change their transfer plans after Eddie Howe's departure from the club

View 2 Images Newcastle United could change their transfer plans after Eddie Howe's exit (Image: Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images)

Newcastle United and Eddie Howe parting ways could provide the perfect opportunity for Ivan Toney to return to St James’ Park. Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle is considered the favourite to replace Howe as Newcastle boss and the 38-year-old has coached Toney for the last two seasons.

‌



The former Brentford star completed a £40million move to the Saudi Pro League in 2024 and has been prolific for Jaissle’s side. Toney, who was included in England’s recent World Cup squad, has scored 72 goals in 93 games for Al-Ahli, helping the club secure back-to-back AFC Champions League triumphs.

‌



Newcastle's strikers struggled for goals last season after making two big-money signings to replace Alexander Isak, with Nick Woltemade fading after an impressive start and Yoane Wissa ending his debut campaign with a solitary league goal. William Osula offered hope as he ended the season with a flourish but the Magpies could potentially look to add more firepower.

‌



It is worth noting that a move for Toney would represent a departure from the club’s current transfer policy, with all four of their summer signings being younger than 21. While there is no suggestion that Newcastle are currently interested in Toney, the experienced striker could prove to be a shrewd addition as Newcastle look to revamp their squad.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Despite moving away from the Premier League, Toney has clearly not lost his goalscoring instincts after finishing last season with 42 goals. He has scored 236 club goals throughout his career, including his three-year spell in the top flight with Brentford, where he memorably hit the 20-goal mark in 2023.

‌



Eddie Howe gets England job verdict as Thomas Tuchel stance taken after Newcastle bombshell READ MORE :

If Jaissle takes Howe’s place in the Newcastle hotseat, the 38-year-old knows how to play to Toney’s strengths. The striker would add another dimension to Newcastle’s striking options and has already proven he can play alongside Wissa.

The pair featured in 71 matches together for Brentford, with Toney scoring 31 and Wissa finding the net on 16 occasions, respectively. Scoring a total 47 goals in 71 games is proof that Newcastle could revive a fruitful attack by bringing Toney back to the club.

The 30-year-old previously joined Newcastle as a teenager in 2015 after making his first team breakthrough at Northampton Town. He ultimately made just four appearances and experienced six loan spells before being sold to Peterborough United in 2018.

‌



View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle has worked with Toney since 2024 (Image: Neville Hopwood/Getty Images)

Returning to the Magpies would signal a full-circle moment for Toney and allow him to finally make his mark at the club. However, it would be more than a sentimental move, with Toney helping to bring the best out of Newcastle’s misfiring attack.

When recently asked about his best position by former Bayern Munich star Thomas Muller, Woltemade said: "Preferably in a two-striker system or behind the striker. It's better for me to play with a lot of freedom and when I have someone around me."

‌



Adding Toney to the Newcastle squad would give the club four senior strikers and the option to create multiple combinations. While Woltemade and Wissa lacked cohesion last term, signing Toney would give the incoming Newcastle boss fresh possibilities.

It remains to be seen whether Jaissle will be appointed Newcastle manager and if the club choose to recruit a striker in the final few weeks of the window. However, with two years left on his Al-Ahli contract, Toney should not be overlooked by Premier League clubs searching for a centre-forward.

Sports.title: Franco Baresi: An all-time great who defined an iconic club and an entire nation
Sports.content:
Franco Baresi: An all-time great who defined an iconic club and an entire nation

Trubutes to the AC Milan and Italy defender have been pouring in after he died at the age of 66 and the game is united in acclaiming him as one of its best defenders

View 3 Images Franco Baresi will be remembered as one of football's greatest-ever defenders

There are good players, great players, players who define a club, players whose charisma has lit up the game. And then, there are players who, somehow, just come to symbolise how a nation plays its football, what its football stands for, what its football is based on.

‌



Johan Cruyff and Holland, Pele and Brazil, Franco Baresi and Italy. It is quite simple. When you think Baresi, you think vintage Italian football.

‌



You think extreme defensive know-how and brilliance. You think ruthless elegance. You think building from the back. You think style.

‌



Baresi, who has passed away at the age of 66, was not just a footballer - he was a way of playing football. He was someone who made the art of defence compelling.

Gianni Infantino facing imminent FIFA wipeout as UEFA could take nuclear option READ MORE :

Baresi was the totem of Italy’s golden footballing generation. He was the totem of the great AC Milan side - managed by Fabio Capello - that went on a 58-game unbeaten league run, earning them the nickname ‘Gli Invincibili’. No translation needed.

The backline of that team read: Paolo Maldini, Alessandro Costacurta, Franco Baresi, Mauro Tassotti. Alexa - define ruthless, define cool, define class.

‌



For those of us from a certain generation, watching those defenders operate was fascinating. Baresi was not a commanding figure but one who exuded such intelligent authority.

He could play as a sweeper, a more conventional centre-half, or even occasionally move into what we now recognise as a pivot in front of the defence. He is one of the greatest defenders in the history of the sport.

View 3 Images AC Milan retired Franco Baresi's shirt after his 20 seasons at the club (Image: AC Milan via Getty Images)

‌



The records show that he was part of the Italian squad that won the World Cup in 1982 but Baresi did not play in that tournament. Instead, of his 81 caps for the national team, his finest two hours came in a losing cause in the 1994 final in Pasadena.

He was 34 and had suffered a meniscus tear in the second game of the group stage against Norway. Yet just over three weeks later, he returned for the final against Brazil.

The game finished goalless after extra-time as Baresi, without injured team-mates Costacurta and Tassotti, put on a display that is widely acknowledged as one of the finest defensive masterclasses in World Cup history. Beset by cramp and fatigue after 120 minutes, Baresi was one of those who missed a penalty in the shootout and played only one more game for his country.

‌



He would carry on playing for his beloved AC Milan, the 1996-97 season being his 20th and last. His number six shirt was retired.

View 3 Images Fabio Capello and Franco Baresi took the great AC Milan side on a 58-game unbeaten league run (Image: Getty Images)

“The entire history of AC Milan is in tears following the passing of Franco Baresi,” the club said. “His example and integrity will be forever etched into the club’s DNA, just as his iconic number six shirt is.”

‌



Baresi won six Serie A titles, three European Cups, two Intercontinental Cups and three European Super Cups. He was runner-up to Milan team-mate Marco van Basten in the 1989 Ballon D’Or vote but individual accolades were a side-issue for Baresi.

It was all about Milan, all about Italy, all about defending. And that will be the special legacy of a truly great player.

Sports.title: 'Genuine concern' expressed for Saltburn members amid 'Clicky Ponting' scandal
Sports.content:
The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League has expressed its "genuine concern for the welfare" of Saltburn Cricket Club members as it continues its inquiry into the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating controversy.

Video footage of a Saltburn player, who has been named as Brian Devine, allegedly clicking his fingers to get a caught-behind wicket in a recent second-team game against Norton sparked outrage and went viral on social media.

The NYSDL launched an investigation on Monday, while Saltburn have suspended Devine for the "foreseeable future" and said they were treating allegations of cheating "with the utmost seriousness".

In a further statement, the League said on Friday that it had met with Saltburn officials and had received guidance from the England and Wales Cricket Board to ensure it follows "a due and appropriate process that has to be comprehensive and fair to all".

Anything less risks prejudicing any formal actions which may follow.

"Finally we would want to place on record our genuine concern for the welfare for those at Saltburn Cricket Club and ask for all to take that into account - there are many people at the club and one of our aims will be to provide them with any well-being support we can."

The video footage was met with global condemnation, with the incident making headlines in Australia, New Zealand, Canada, India and the USA among other countries, while it has been dubbed 'Clicky Ponting' in reference to former Australia captain Ricky Ponting.

Saltburn, 17 points clear at the top of Division Two after winning the match by 159 runs, conceded Wednesday's second-team cup match against Marton in the wake of the controversy.

In response to the video footage on social media, Middlesbrough's second XI captain Rory Cotterill claimed there were two more incidents of cheating in his side's 29-run defeat to Saltburn last month.

Image: Saltburn Cricket Club is at the centre of the sporting scandal

More video footage has since emerged, which allegedly shows Devine, then playing for Pudsey St Lawrence in the Bradford Premier League, repeatedly clicking his fingers while opponents were batting.

Pudsey St Lawrence said in a statement on Thursday: "At no stage was the club aware of any alleged misconduct by Mr Devine, nor were any concerns or complaints raised with the club by opposition teams or umpires who officiated the fixtures in question.

"The club expects its players to uphold the highest standards of integrity and sportsmanship and takes any credible concerns extremely seriously."

The Bradford League added in a statement: "We are aware of the video footage circulating, but it is not our policy to undertake retrospective investigations."

Sports.title: 'It would be a brilliant story' - Key open to Stokes making Ashes return
Sports.content:
England cricket chief Rob Key has left the door open to Ben Stokes coming out of international retirement to play in next summer's home Ashes series against Australia.

Stokes gave up the England Test captaincy and retired from international cricket following his side's 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand in June, which followed a 4-1 Ashes loss to Australia over the winter.

The 35-year-old's decision came after he had been made unavailable for selection for the second Test against New Zealand, after breaching a midnight curfew when out celebrating England's win in the series opener.

There was speculation in the aftermath of the saga that Stokes had been left disappointed by the way he was treated by England's hierarchy, who on Thursday reinstated Joe Root as captain and appointed Stephen Fleming as Brendon McCullum's successor as Test head coach.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stokes reflected on his England career after his final Test match

Asked if the door was still open to Stokes returning to face Australia next summer, England managing director Key told Sky Sports News: "It would be a brilliant story if he does."

Quizzed on whether Stokes had intimated a return, Key said: "No, he hasn't but I wouldn't be surprised. Anything's possible with Ben."

On whether the bridge had been burnt in terms of his own relationship with Stokes, Key added: "No, not at all. Not as far as I'm concerned."

Key: I'm still the right man for the job

Image: Key reasserted his passion to continue leading English cricket after a run of seven defeats in the last nine Tests

Key also reaffirmed his desire to continue in his own position, which has come under scrutiny during a turbulent summer for English Test cricket.

England's managing director has overseen the sacking of a head coach, the retirement of a captain, a plethora of behavioural issues amid allegations of a drinking culture and a run of seven losses in the last nine Test matches.

Asked whether he still had the passion to lead England cricket, Key said: "Yeah, definitely.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day five of the third Test between England and New Zealand

"I'm optimistic about what we can do.

"The players that are going to take us forward into this next generation are the ones I believe that can go on to become world-class cricketers. There's a couple in there at the moment. There's so many that could go on to become a world-class team

"The key now is to not only have success but sustain it and keep repeating it. That's the system we're trying to put in place.

"In Stephen Fleming and Brendon McCullum, I think we've got the best two coaches"

Fleming's lack of red-ball experience not a concern, says Key

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Key explains why former New Zealand captain Stephen Fleming has been selected as head coach of the England Test side

Key also batted away doubts over incoming head coach Fleming's lack of experience with international or red-ball cricket.

Fleming's sole head coaching role since retiring as New Zealand Test captain has been at the helm of the Chennai Super Kings in the IPL, recently vacating the post he has held since 2009 before taking on the England job.

"I think he's [been] one of the most experienced coaches of international cricketers for the last 18 years," said Key.

"You think about that job that he's done in the IPL and you do not forget Test cricket, how to go about it, how to play it with the career that he had as a player, more importantly as a captain as well.

"It's not like for the last 18 years whilst he's been in the IPL he's not been across Test cricket. We've had dealings in the past when our players have gone to Chennai and they've all spoken so highly - I've not met anyone that hasn't spoken highly about Stephen Fleming as a coach.

"I think he's hugely experienced in not only the franchise world, dealing with international cricketers and dealing with Test cricket in particular."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fleming scored an unbeaten 66 in the first innings of the deciding Test as he captained New Zealand to a 2-1 series win in 1999, which saw England fall to last place in the rankings. Can he reverse their fortunes now as Test head coach?

Key also advocated refining an already-established approach to Test cricket, rather than making rash changes to the progress made by the Test team under Stokes and McCullum.

"This is a team now that has lost an entire generation of cricketers bar Joe Root," he said.

"We've had to rebuild the bowling attack. They've lost over a thousand wickets in the last few years and there is so much potential there.

"I believe Stephen Fleming is the best person to get the basics bowlers running and consistently hitting a line and length with all of that potential, all the attributes that they have.

"A refined approach is needed, not a change of approach."

Sports.title: Stavley, Ghodoussi company makes offer for West Ham stake
Sports.content:
Amanda Staveley and husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi's PCP Capital Partners have made an offer to buy a 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham.

Sky News' Mark Kleinman broke the news on Thursday that the couple were preparing a bid for a share that belongs to the family of the late David Gold. That offer has now gone in.

Sky News also reported that the club's current investors have first refusal on whether they would like to match the offer.

Sources close to the situation insisted to Sky News that Daniel Kretinsky, who raised his share in the club earlier this year, remains interested in a deal.

However, West Ham's ownership structure means he does not want to acquire all of the Gold-owned stake, which would make him the club's majority owner.

If there is an agreement with both parties, the Gold family will make a statement - not PCP - out of respect to all other shareholders.

Image: The family of the late David Gold currently own the 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham

Sky Sports News understands there will be no public comment from PCP for the same reason while negotiations are ongoing.

Staveley and PCP have held discussions with a number of Premier League clubs since leaving Newcastle, including Tottenham, but are now focused on the Hammers.

What has happened at West Ham so far this summer?

It has been a busy summer for West Ham after their relegation from the Premier League. There were questions over whether Nuno Espirito Santo would continue as head coach - and it was soon confirmed that he would.

Joint-chairman David Sullivan also stepped down after "serious historic allegations" emerged regarding his conduct, which he denies.

In terms of transfers, Matheus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville have been the biggest outgoings. But perhaps their best bit of business will be keeping captain Jarrod Bowen.

It was also reported on Friday that West Ham are in talks with Celtic for midfielder Arne Engels.

Sports.title: AC Milan and Italy legend Baresi dies aged 66
Sports.content:
Former AC Milan and Italy defender Franco Baresi has died aged 66.

The former Milan captain is widely regarded as one of the finest defenders in football history and spent his entire career with the club, playing 719 times in 20 seasons as a professional.

During that time Baresi won six Serie A crowns, with his first Scudetto coming as a teenager during the 1978-79 campaign and he lifted five further titles in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
