World.title: Japan Tops Global Waste Index 2025; U.S., Israel, and Chile Rank as Worst Polluters
World.content:
Japan has emerged as the world leader in waste management, while Israel, Chile, and the United States rank among the worst-performing countries, according to the Global Waste Index 2025 released by Slovak-based waste technology company Sensoneo.

The report, which ranks all 38 OECD member states based on their waste generation and disposal practices, highlights significant disparities in global waste management. Sensoneoâs index evaluates countries on per capita waste generation, recycling, incineration, and landfill use.

Israel and Chile ranked last and second-to-last, respectively, primarily due to their heavy reliance on environmentally damaging landfilling practices. Israel sends 524 of the 650 kilograms of waste it generates per person each year directly to landfills. Chile recycles just 1% of its waste and sends more than 95% to landfill.

The United States, which increased its per capita waste generation from 811 to 951 kilograms since 2022, remains the highest generator of municipal solid waste globally. The U.S. disposes of nearly half of that â 447 kilograms â in landfills annually. Neighboring Canada also performed poorly, landfilling 67% of its annual 694 kg per capita waste.

At the other end of the spectrum, Japan ranked No. 1, followed by South Korea and Estonia, all of which combine relatively low waste generation with efficient disposal methods. Japan sends only 3 kilograms per capita to landfill, relying heavily on incineration (245 kg) and maintaining a controlled recycling rate.

European countries dominated the top 10 rankings, with Austria, Germany, Finland, Belgium, Sweden, Norway, and Switzerland all demonstrating strong waste management systems. Austria topped the recycling chart with 334 kilograms of municipal waste recycled per person annually â accounting for 42% of its total waste.

Meanwhile, Spain fell four places to 27th despite minor improvements. The country reduced its landfill and incineration rates slightly while increasing recycling by 10 kilograms per capita. However, its overall waste generation rose by 10 kg compared to the 2022 index.

The index revealed that in 12 of the 38 countries, over half of all waste is still landfilled â including in developed nations like Australia, New Zealand, and Canada. By contrast, Switzerland was the only country to report zero landfill disposal, while Belgium, Finland, Estonia, and Japan landfilled less than 3 kg per person.

Other key findings include:

New Zealand , Finland , and Iceland posted the largest reductions in waste generation per capita.

, , and posted the largest reductions in waste generation per capita. From an environmental standpoint, incineration is considered preferable to landfilling, but excessive reliance on either suggests a need for stronger waste reduction and recycling strategies.

About the Index and Sensoneo

First launched in 2019, the Global Waste Index is published every three years by Sensoneo, a company specializing in digital transformation for waste management systems. The 2025 edition is based on the latest available national data.

Sensoneo operates in 87 countries and provides waste monitoring solutions to cities, industries, and governments. It is the only company to have successfully implemented deposit return systems (DRS) IT infrastructure in nine countries, achieving recycling rates above 90%.

In Madrid, Sensoneo is deploying 11,100 smart sensors, marking the worldâs largest smart waste monitoring installation to date.

World.title: South Korean Model and Actor Kim Jong Suk Dies at 29, Family Urges Respect Amid Speculation
World.content:
South Korean model and television personality Kim Jong Suk has died at the age of 29, his family confirmed on June 6. The news has shocked fans and colleagues across the countryâs entertainment industry, where Kim rose to prominence following his appearance on tvNâs 2022 reality dating show Skip Dating.

Kim, who began his career in modeling before transitioning to television, had been steadily gaining popularity in recent years. His sudden death has prompted an outpouring of grief and speculation online.

While the exact cause of death remains unconfirmed, some media reports have linked Kimâs passing to an incident in Hanam involving a violent altercation between a young man and his girlfriend. According to the reports, law enforcement responded to the scene, after which the man allegedly died by suicide after jumping from a high-rise building.

Amid widespread online discussion and conjecture, Kimâs family issued a public plea for restraint, asking the public and media to refrain from spreading misinformation or making disrespectful assumptions.

Kimâs older sister posted on social media, expressing the family’s devastation and emotional exhaustion. âWe ask for privacy and understanding during this difficult time,â she wrote, emphasizing the familyâs wish to grieve in peace.

Details regarding funeral arrangements have not been made public.

World.title: Fernández de Kirchner asks UN to suspend the ban keeping her off the ballot
World.content:
Fernández de Kirchner asks UN to suspend the ban keeping her off the ballot

31st Friday, July 2026 - 09:39 UTC Full article

Fernández de Kirchner, 73, was sentenced to six years in prison and permanent disqualification from public office for fraud in the awarding of public works contracts during her terms

The defense team of former Argentine president Cristina Fernández de Kirchner has filed an individual communication with the United Nations Human Rights Committee seeking suspension of the lifetime ban on holding public office imposed on her by the Argentine courts, her lawyers announced on Wednesday in Buenos Aires.

The filing includes three precautionary measures: provisionally lifting the disqualification, restoring the Supreme Court to its five members — it currently operates with three — and modifying her house arrest regime, including removal of her electronic ankle monitor. The defense also requested a full review of the conviction.

Fernández de Kirchner, 73, who served as president from 2007 to 2015, was sentenced to six years in prison and permanent disqualification from public office for fraud in the awarding of public works contracts during her terms. The sentence became final after being upheld by the Supreme Court, and she has been under house arrest since 2025.

The team comprises Argentina's Carlos Beraldi, Spain's Javier Borrego — a former judge of Spain's Supreme Court and of the European Court of Human Rights — and Brazil's Rafael Valim, who took part in Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's submission to the same committee during the proceedings stemming from the Lava Jato investigation.

The lawyers argue that the trial violated guarantees set out in the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, a treaty with constitutional rank in Argentina, and say a permanent sanction contradicts the body's earlier findings. Valim said the precautionary request seeks suspension of a sanction that he argues runs counter to clear committee precedent. The allegations of judicial arbitrariness and persecution made by the defense and by the former president herself have not been independently substantiated.

In an interview on Thursday, Valim said the committee's decisions are binding and form part of Argentina's commitments before the United Nations. The mechanism, however, is not equivalent to an enforceable judgment: if the committee finds a rights violation, it issues recommendations for the state to adopt remedial measures, without means of compulsory enforcement. The lawyer also noted that Argentina's Federal Criminal Procedure Code provides for such a decision as grounds to review a final sentence.

Valim estimated the precautionary measures could be resolved within months and the merits could take years. He also argued that winning a primary election does not amount to holding public office, meaning the disqualification would not bar a candidacy, while acknowledging that this reading is contested. Whether the primary system will be in force for 2027 has not been settled.

In a letter circulated on social media, Fernández de Kirchner said the disqualification is in fact the principal penalty. Her son, lawmaker Máximo Kirchner, said the Peronist movement wants her as its 2027 candidate, in a field that also includes Buenos Aires province Governor Axel Kicillof.

World.title: Stability alone does not buy a house: Georgieva's message in Montevideo
World.content:
Stability alone does not buy a house: Georgieva's message in Montevideo

31st Friday, July 2026 - 08:02 UTC Full article

Stability cannot be put in a refrigerator, she said, and a house cannot be bought on stability alone: more growth is genuinely needed

International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva praised Uruguay's macroeconomic and institutional strength on Thursday but urged authorities to take greater risks to turn that stability into growth.

Stability cannot be put in a refrigerator, she said, and a house cannot be bought on stability alone: more growth is genuinely needed. She was speaking at the annual economics conference organized by the Central Bank of Uruguay. In closing, she called for protecting what has been achieved while adding a little more courage to face the new international environment.

Georgieva highlighted the social consensus underpinning Uruguayan policy and described it as an asset in an increasingly polarized world. She noted that the country holds public debt of around 60% of gross domestic product and an electricity matrix that is 98% renewable. Among areas with potential she identified logistics capacity to serve neighboring countries, greater cost efficiency in public services, simplified procedures for small and medium-sized enterprises, and preparing society for the impact of artificial intelligence.

On monetary policy, she welcomed the reduction of inflation to 4.5% and the anchoring of expectations, but advised against rushing to set a lower target while external shocks persist, particularly on energy prices. She also backed the central bank's de-dollarization strategy, arguing that wider use of the national currency strengthens the capacity to respond to shocks the country cannot control, and recommended encouraging peso savings through better returns.

Central bank Governor Guillermo Tolosa had warned on Wednesday that Uruguayans' financial decisions remain shaped by fear inherited from the 2002 crisis. Georgieva compared that behavior with the experience of Bulgaria, her home country.

Turning to the global context, the IMF chief described a transition from a predictable order toward a system with multiple centers of gravity, and warned that protectionism and trade fragmentation could cut as much as 7% of world output. The fund projects global inflation of 4.7% this year and holds that a resurgence would raise debt servicing costs. She cited the conflict in the Middle East and tensions in the Strait of Hormuz among sources of vulnerability. On artificial intelligence, she estimated it could add up to 0.8 percentage points to annual global growth, while affecting 40% of jobs worldwide and as much as 60% in advanced economies.

Georgieva said Latin America has a unique opportunity to realize its potential through greater regional integration. Economy Minister Gabriel Oddone described the visit as a political one.

World.title: British journalist suggests channeling Enzo Fernández's taxes to Falklands defense
World.content:
British journalist suggests channeling Enzo Fernández's taxes to Falklands defense

30th Thursday, July 2026 - 23:08 UTC Full article

Winter made the suggestion on a television program hosted by Piers Morgan

British sports journalist Henry Winter has proposed that the taxes Argentine footballer Enzo Fernández pays in the United Kingdom be directed toward the defense of the Falklands, as a form of punishment after FIFA opened disciplinary proceedings against the Argentine Football Association.

Winter made the suggestion on a television program hosted by Piers Morgan. He said that were he in the British government, he would propose transferring the player's tax contribution, which he estimated at more than two million pounds a year, to the Islands for residents to decide how to spend it. The figure is Winter's own estimate of the footballer's private finances and has not been verified. The remarks were an opinion offered on a television show: there is no indication that the British government or FIFA is considering any such measure.

Fernández, however, is not among those charged. The proceedings opened by the Disciplinary Committee on July 29 cover Leandro Paredes, Nahuel Molina, Thiago Almada, assistant coach Roberto Ayala and Spain's Gavi, along with the AFA. The Chelsea midfielder was sent off during the final for two bookings, near the end of regulation time, and not for the incidents that followed the final whistle.

Winter also questioned the effectiveness of a financial penalty, arguing it would be negligible against the revenue Argentina earned from its run in the tournament, and proposed stripping Argentina of the match it has been allocated in the centenary edition of the 2030 World Cup. Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay will each host one game of that edition; the remaining matches will be played in Spain, Portugal and Morocco. Morgan, for his part, had posted a message after the semifinal containing a crude insult aimed at the Argentine squad and a reference to the outcome of the 1982 war.

The case against the AFA concerns four articles of the Disciplinary Code, among them the use of a sporting event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, and discrimination. FIFA cited allegedly discriminatory chanting and gestures, delayed kickoffs, failure to comply with protocols and the display of inappropriate messages. Those charged will be able to present their positions before a ruling.

The banner reading “Las Malvinas son argentinas” was displayed on July 16 in Atlanta, after Argentina's 2-1 semifinal win over England. There is a direct precedent: in 2014 FIFA fined the AFA 30,000 Swiss francs for unfurling the same message before a friendly against Slovenia.

Argentina claims sovereignty over the archipelago, which is a British overseas territory. In a 2013 referendum, islanders voted overwhelmingly to retain that status.

World.title: From closing the central bank to reforming it: Milei's shift on monetary authority
World.content:
From closing the central bank to reforming it: Milei's shift on monetary authority

30th Thursday, July 2026 - 23:05 UTC Full article

The core of the bill is a ban on direct and indirect financing of the state by the institution

Argentine President Javier Milei presented on Thursday, in a nationwide broadcast, a bill to overhaul the central bank's charter, the statute governing the monetary authority, in an initiative the government considers central to its economic program and which it will send to the Chamber of Deputies in the coming days.

The core of the bill is a ban on direct and indirect financing of the state by the institution. It envisages eliminating temporary advances to the Treasury, restricting purchases of government paper in the primary market and scrapping non-transferable notes, the mechanism through which the Treasury obtained dollars from reserves in exchange for securities that cannot be traded. It would also cap transfers of accounting profits: gains arising from asset revaluation would go into a technical reserve rather than fund current spending.

The initiative additionally seeks to reverse the reform passed in 2012 under Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, which broadened the institution's objectives to include financial stability, employment and economic development with social equity, and loosened the mechanisms for assisting the Treasury. The government argues that this multiplicity of objectives allowed successive administrations to finance the deficit through money printing. Milei has criticized in personal terms Mercedes Marcó del Pont, who headed the central bank when that amendment was approved.

The bill would also tighten the requirements for removing the bank's president and board members, which according to circulated accounts would require two-thirds of the votes in both chambers. The charter currently in force is Law 24,144, enacted in 1992.

The proposal marks a shift from the position Milei held as a candidate, when he repeatedly called for abolishing the central bank, which he blamed for Argentine inflation. In office, he opted instead for an institutional reform narrowing its functions and barring it from financing the Treasury. The president has framed the initiative as ending what he called 91 years of fraud, referring to the institution's creation in 1935.

Those involved in drafting the bill include Economy Minister Luis Caputo; central bank President Santiago Bausili; and Deregulation Minister Federico Sturzenegger, who headed the institution between 2015 and 2018. The reform is part of an economic package that, according to Argentine press reports, would also include a zero-deficit fiscal rule. To pass it, the government will need to negotiate with allied blocs and sections of the opposition.

World.title: Milei decree allows expulsion of foreigners over hate messages against Argentina
World.content:
Milei decree allows expulsion of foreigners over hate messages against Argentina

30th Thursday, July 2026 - 18:59 UTC Full article

Whoever attacks the Argentine Republic is not welcome in the country, the Office of the President said in announcing the measure

Argentine President Javier Milei has signed an emergency decree allowing authorities to bar entry, cancel residence permits already granted and expel foreigners who direct or incite expressions of hatred, discrimination or violence on grounds of nationality, as well as those who desecrate national symbols.

The measure, Decree 681/2026, was published on Thursday in the Official Gazette and amends the Migration Law. In its rationale, the government states that hate messages and acts of hostility and contempt directed at the Argentine people, their culture and their national identity have increased considerably, and that such conduct poses a risk to social peace. The text specifies that the provision may not be applied to expressions of ideological dissent or to political, academic or civic criticism that constitutes a legitimate exercise of constitutional rights.

Whoever attacks the Argentine Republic is not welcome in the country, the Office of the President said in announcing the measure, which it linked to recent displays of hostility toward Argentina.

The decree follows the controversy that erupted on social media during and after the World Cup held in the United States, Mexico and Canada, in which Argentina lost the final to Spain. The criticism that circulated ranged from claims of favorable refereeing for the Argentine team to accusations of racism.

Milei said on July 26 that the Brazilian government financed 25% of that alleged campaign, with backing from Mexico and the US Democratic Party. He offered no evidence and the accusations remain unsubstantiated. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum denied that her government promoted any such campaign. Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno cited on Wednesday, as part of the phenomenon, posts by Spanish singer Rosalía — who arrived in Buenos Aires on Thursday for a series of concerts — and actors Samuel L. Jackson and Javier Bardem.

The measure drew legal and political objections. Constitutional scholar Félix Lonigro said restrictions of this kind must conform to the principle of legality and be legislated by Congress. Former Justice Minister Mariano Cúneo Libarona, who backed the measure in general terms, questioned its vagueness and urged that it not become a selective tool. Deputy Maximiliano Ferraro, of the Coalición Cívica, called it unconstitutional, and former national migration director Florencia Carignano noted that if other countries applied equivalent criteria, Milei himself would be barred from several.

The episode follows insults Milei directed on Saturday, July 25, in São Paulo at the Brazilian president and at a Supreme Federal Court justice, including a slur about the judge's physical appearance, which led Brazil to recall its ambassador in Buenos Aires for consultations.

World.title: Brazil confirms its ambassador will return to Buenos Aires but sets no date
World.content:
Brazil confirms its ambassador will return to Buenos Aires but sets no date

30th Thursday, July 2026 - 16:26 UTC Full article

The crisis erupted when Argentine President Javier Milei spoke at the Liberal Party's national convention in São Paulo, where he backed Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy

The Brazilian government confirmed that its ambassador to Argentina, Julio Glinternick Bitelli, will return to Buenos Aires after being recalled for consultations, without specifying when, in the first sign of de-escalation in the most serious diplomatic crisis between the two countries in decades.

Sources at Itamaraty said the underlying decision has been taken and that the timing of the return will depend on how the bilateral climate evolves. Accounts differ, however, on the scope of that determination: while some reports hold that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has already given political authorization, others published the same Thursday indicate that Brasília will keep the diplomat away from Buenos Aires indefinitely, pending signs of moderation from the Argentine government.

Bitelli, ambassador since 2023, arrived in Brasília on Monday and held two rounds of meetings with Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira, the second on Wednesday, followed by a meeting with Lula.

The crisis erupted on Saturday, July 25, when Argentine President Javier Milei spoke at the Liberal Party's national convention in São Paulo, where he backed Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy for the October 4 election. In his speech he called Lula a convict and directed an insult about the physical appearance of Supreme Federal Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, who had denied him authorization to visit Jair Bolsonaro, imprisoned over the attempted coup.

The following day, on Radio Mitre, Milei said the Brazilian government supplied 25% of the resources for an alleged campaign against Argentina waged on social media during the World Cup held in the United States, and extended the accusation to Mexico and the US Democratic Party. He offered no evidence for those claims, which remain unsubstantiated.

Vieira described the episode as unprecedented and, in addition to recalling Bitelli, summoned Argentine Ambassador Daniel Raimondi. Lula issued a statement defending Brazil as a democratic and sovereign country and saying it is unacceptable for a foreign head of state to address Brazilian institutions disrespectfully. Other members of the Brazilian government responded with personal insults directed at the Argentine leader.

The first conciliatory signal came from Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno, who ruled out any break in relations. There is no chance relations will be broken from the Argentine side, he said, adding that his government holds Bitelli in the highest esteem and hopes for his swift return to continue the bilateral agenda. Officials in Brasília read those words as separating the two presidents' political differences from the state-to-state relationship.

The antagonism dates back to 2023, when Lula publicly backed Sergio Massa during the Argentine campaign. Brazil is Argentina's main trading partner. According to the latest Datafolha poll, Lula leads by five points in a potential runoff.

World.title: Falklands suspend new permanent residence applications for up to 12 months
World.content:
Falklands suspend new permanent residence applications for up to 12 months

30th Thursday, July 2026 - 15:11 UTC Full article

The measure applies to applications made under section 18 of the Immigration Ordinance 1999

The Falkland Islands Executive Council has approved a temporary suspension of new applications for Permanent Residence Permits (PRP) for a period of up to 12 months, while a full review of the system is carried out, the Legislative Assembly said in a public statement on Thursday.

The measure applies to applications made under section 18 of the Immigration Ordinance 1999. The review will cover the points-based assessment framework and the annual quota of permits, and its findings, together with any recommended changes, will be brought back to Executive Council for a decision.

The statement says the system was last substantially revised in 2021, following an extended period of consultation and policy development. Those changes broadened access to permanent residence and, according to the Falkland Islands Government, led to a significant increase in the number of applications made and permits granted each year. The statement does not provide figures to support that assessment.

Assembly members have asked that the regime now be reviewed to ensure it continues to operate in the long-term interests of the Islands and that the granting of permanent residence remains tied to a “meaningful and lasting contribution” to the territory. The review will consider whether the current assessment criteria and annual quota remain the right ones in light of the Islands' economic and population objectives.

The suspension applies only to new applications and does not affect anyone who already holds a PRP. Those who had anticipated applying this year will need to apply to extend their existing permit or for a new permit, as applicable, through the usual processes. The Falkland Islands Government said it has made arrangements to deal with any of its employees who might be directly affected, and added that other employers will need to consider whether they need to take action as a result.

The statement does not specify the date from which the suspension takes effect, nor how it fits with the start of the quota year, traditionally set at 2 September.

The measure is different in nature from the suspensions reported in September 2023 and April 2024, which stemmed from the available quota being exhausted and lifted automatically at the start of a new period. On this occasion the pause follows a policy decision while the regime as a whole is examined.

The PRP is granted through a points-based assessment that weighs factors including employment, income, work experience, educational and professional qualifications and assets, and requires a minimum of three years' residence, criminal record checks and health and educational assessments for dependents. It is also a prerequisite for Falkland Islands status, which is granted to those who can demonstrate seven years of ordinary residence.

Cultural diversity

The review follows two decades of demographic change. With a population of around 3,700, the Falklands are now home to people of 68 nationalities, according to a 2025 report. Alongside those who identify as Falkland Islanders or British, the largest contingents come from the Philippines, Zimbabwe, Chile and St Helena, with smaller groups from Australia, Canada, New Zealand and the United States. The population has doubled over forty years, and the growth recorded since 2010 has been driven by employment in fields including healthcare, education, policing, public administration, tourism and catering.

That growth has taken place within a framework that prioritizes the local labor market: the Immigration (General) Regulations 2021 strengthened the requirement that vacancies be advertised to residents before being offered abroad. In parallel, the charity Multicultural Falklands organizes cultural and culinary events open to the whole community, among them a Multicultural Day and a Festival of Lights. The PRP is the mechanism that turns that labor migration into settled residence, placing the announced review at the center of decisions about the future size and composition of the population.

World.title: Bolivia issues arrest order against Morales over May and June road blockades
World.content:
Bolivia issues arrest order against Morales over May and June road blockades

30th Thursday, July 2026 - 06:37 UTC Full article

Morales rejected the accusations, describing them as political persecution and an attempt to divert attention from the country's economic crisis

The Santa Cruz departmental prosecutor's office issued an arrest order on Wednesday against former president Evo Morales (2006-2019) over his alleged role in the road blockades and protests that paralyzed parts of Bolivia for 53 days in May and June.

The document, signed by prosecutor Brayan Melgar Ledezma of the specialized corruption prosecution unit, names Morales and other unidentified individuals in connection with six alleged offenses: armed uprising against the security and sovereignty of the state, terrorism, endangering the safety of transportation, criminal association, public incitement to commit crimes, and endangering the safety of public services. The investigation stems from a complaint filed by the Pro Santa Cruz Civic Committee, later joined by the Interior Ministry.

Morales rejected the accusations, describing them as political persecution and an attempt to divert attention from the country's economic crisis. He wrote on the social network X that his position has always been clear, that he stands with those suffering from austerity, fuel shortages, the rising cost of living, insecurity and the spread of drug trafficking, and that he will not be intimidated. He posted from the Chapare, the tropical region of Cochabamba where he remains under the protection of coca growers' organizations.

The purpose of the protests is disputed. The complaint holds that they sought President Rodrigo Paz's resignation; Morales says they demanded socioeconomic measures from the government rather than the president's departure. Morales himself posted on May 24 that Paz had two options in the crisis: militarize the country or call elections within 90 days.

The protests began among Aymara farming organizations in La Paz and labor unions demanding greater say in government decisions, and kept the administrative capital under blockade for nearly two months. Spain's El País reported 22 deaths, a figure that has not been independently corroborated; when the pacification agreement was signed on June 20, the toll reported at the time was 14.

The charges also cover the head of the Bolivian Workers' Central, Argollo, and La Paz farm leader Vicente Salazar, who has been in pretrial detention since July 6. The union leader's case is sensitive for the government: he was the chief negotiator of the June agreement with Paz, which according to the same source included respecting union immunity and dropping legal proceedings against members of the labor federation.

Morales also faces an arrest order in force since October 2024 for failing to appear in a case involving the alleged abuse of a minor, a matter that remains unresolved and whose charges he denies, attributing them to political motives. Authorities have been criticized for not enforcing that order.

World.title: Puebla thieves make off with a million pesos from a currency exchange in a heist worthy of Netflix
World.content:
A theft at a currency exchange in Puebla has made national headlines thanks to the criminals’ method, reminiscent of formulaic heist movies.

The crime took place Sunday night in the Santa Cruz Buenavista neighborhood of Puebla city. A group of thieves drilled a hole to enter the facility, bypassed the security systems and escaped with an estimated 1 million pesos (US $57,616).

It wasn’t until the next morning that employees discovered the theft and notified security authorities after finding a hole that reached the bathroom area.

Sunday’s theft was the second experienced by the same currency exchange in less than a month, a coincidence — or not — that has roused the suspicions of investigators.

It has also prompted social media users to compare it to the heist in the Netflix TV show “La Casa de Papel,” which recounts the real-life events of a robbery of the Spanish mint house.

How did the robbery happen?

According to initial reports, the criminals acted at night, wearing clothing that made identification difficult.

They first entered a physiotherapy clinic next to the currency exchange, whose wall connects to the adjacent premises.

From there, they drilled through the wall that led to the exchange’s restrooms, allowing them to enter undetected.

Once inside, the perpetrators removed a door and used it to block the view of the interior security cameras, which allowed them to move through the area where the cash was stored and steal the loot without triggering the main alarms.

Officials from the Puebla State Attorney General’s Office are working to obtain physical evidence, analyze the route the criminals used, and review available video surveillance cameras from both the currency exchange and nearby properties.

Authorities have not yet released the number of criminals involved in the robbery, who still remain at large.

With reports from Eje Central and NMás

World.title: Inside the massive cheating scandal shaking UNAM, Mexico’s top university
World.content:
“Scandal at UNAM.”

“Mexican university faces massive cheating scandal after first online entry exam.”

“158,000 exams under scrutiny: The biggest public university in Mexico investigates the use of AI to cheat.”

“UNAM: Was artificial intelligence to blame?”

These are some of the headlines that have appeared in the media in recent days amid intense and growing scrutiny of the results of the National Autonomous University of Mexico’s entrance exams, which were published earlier this month.

In this explainer, we’ll tell you everything you need to know about this “scandal,” which has also been widely referred to as a “crisis” for UNAM, Mexico’s largest and most prestigious university.

UNAM’s cheating scandal, explained

In May and June, UNAM held its exams for people vying to become students at the university, whose main campus, Ciudad Universitaria (University City), is located in southern Mexico City.

The university’s entrance exams have previously been held in large auditoriums and stadiums, but in 2026 — for the first time ever — would-be UNAM students completed the tests online. One aim of moving exams online was to save aspirants the time and money involved in traveling to an exam center. Another was to make the exams more accessible to aspirants across the country and even abroad.

More than 158,000 aspirants sat the online exams. Among them were people hoping to gain entry to high-demand UNAM degree programs that are notoriously hard to get into, such as medicine and law.

The software for the exams was provided by the Mexican company Territorium Life. It had a range of AI-powered built-in features designed to prevent test-takers from cheating — including one that prevented additional computer tabs from being opened — but there is widespread suspicion that a significant number of them did indeed cheat, including by using artificial intelligence platforms such as ChatGPT.

None of the software’s in-built features could physically stop people from using a second computer or a smartphone while sitting their UNAM entrance exams, although it was equipped with a camera and microphone-assisted surveillance system designed to detect irregular — i.e., deceitful — conduct.

Territorium Life said that its exam platform “operated as planned.”

Around 2% of exams have already been nullified because the software’s surveillance system, overseen by a group of human behavior experts, detected cheating.

Suspicious entrance exam results

UNAM published the results of its admission exams on July 17. The first suspicions about them emerged on social media, according to the newspaper El País.

Why were the results suspicious? In a nutshell, because they were unusually good.

In the past, the percentage of test-takers who responded correctly to more than 100 questions on 120-question multiple-choice exams was below 10%.

In 2025, the percentage of test-takers who got more than 100 questions correct on the medicine degree entrance exam was 9%. The figure this year was 29.3%.

Almost 19% of law degree candidates got more than 100 questions correct in 2026, up from just 3.7% last year. The figure for would-be UNAM science degree students rose to 30.4% from 9.7% a year earlier.

The higher incidence of excellent exam results “drastically increased the required thresholds to enter” UNAM degree programs, the BBC reported.

🎓⚠️ Especialistas alertan sobre posibles irregularidades en el examen virtual de ingreso a licenciatura de la UNAM. Tras publicarse los resultados, se detectó un aumento atípico de aspirantes con puntajes superiores a 100 aciertos: mientras en años anteriores representaban… pic.twitter.com/y9h1LXahGw — LuisCardenasMX (@LuisCardenasMx) July 21, 2026

The cheating allegations

The allegations that some people cheated in their UNAM entrance exams are, at this stage at least, exactly that — allegations. Nothing has yet been proven.

However, the widespread suspicion is that some, or perhaps many, aspirants used AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude while completing their exams.

The news outlet Infobae reported that before the various UNAM entrance exams were held, videos on the social media platform TikTok provided a “cheating instruction manual.”

Among the advice offered on TikTok was to have “ChatGPT running on a second monitor outside the [camera’s] frame,” Infobae reported.

A test-taker could conceivably have been assisted by a second person outside the camera’s view who held up AI-generated answers on a laptop, for example.

Eduardo Backhoff, a Mexican psychologist and education assessment expert, wrote on social media that “either the exams were easier [than in previous years], the students were smarter, or they cheated.”

“The first two possibilities are highly unlikely; the last one is the only plausible explanation. In this case, those who don’t deserve it are being rewarded,” he wrote.

In a radio report, NPR journalist Eyder Peralta said that “Raul Rojas, who teaches AI at the Free University of Berlin and statistics at the University of Nevada, Reno, says when he looked at all the test scores, he didn’t find the kind of deviation you can chalk up to an easier test or perhaps a smarter class.”

Rojas told NPR that his conclusion was that “almost half of the students were cheating when taking the exam online.”

Peralta said that the tests “were open for 17 days, giving ample chance for friends or internet entrepreneurs to leak or sell test questions.”

“Blind spots in technology also allowed students to have someone else take their test,” he said.

UNAM’s response

UNAM has launched an investigation into the suspected cheating by some exam candidates and suspended the enrollment of new students shortly before the new academic year is scheduled to begin.

The university’s rector, Leonardo Lomelí Vanegas, has named a group of 16 experts in fields including education, AI and law, to examine what happened. Backhoff is a member of that group, which is expected to complete its investigation promptly.

Lomelí, UNAM rector since late 2023, said that fair access to the university’s degree programs cannot be compromised by “those aspirants who may have had some kind of help.”

He also said that none of the possible responses to the alleged cheating are ruled out — i.e., there is a chance that the exam results will be nullified and UNAM aspirants will have to sit entrance exams again.

If the results were nullified, would-be UNAM students who studied hard and did well in their exams without cheating would be unfairly penalized. However, having aspirants re-sit the exams — in person — may be the only way to ensure that the admission process is fair for everyone.

The university’s decision “could set legal, technological, educational and evaluative precedents,” said Juan Manuel Flores Ayala, an education assessment expert who was quoted in the El País newspaper.

“… I would lean toward repeating the exam and moving the semester as needed to restore credibility and provide certainty to the people UNAM serves as a public institution. There is a political and legal cost to doing so, but I think more would be gained than lost,” Flores said.

UNAM, BBC reported, also announced that it filed criminal complaints against “people and companies that offer fraudulent services” related to its entrance exams.

The university is dealing with an issue faced by education institutes around the world — students’ use (including improper and fraudulent use) of AI.

Aspirants’ views

Some UNAM aspirants have protested to demand that the exams be held again. Others want the results to stand.

In the aforementioned NPR radio report, protesting test-takers can be heard chanting, “We want honesty, not artificial intelligence.”

At Ciudad Universitaria, they also demanded that an “examen presencial,” or in-person exam, be held for UNAM aspirants.

One would-be applied mathematics student, Leonardo Ruiz, told NPR that his exam results had already been invalidated.

“He assumes his exam was flagged for cheating because he scored too well, but he says he did it by studying,” NPR’s Eyder Peralta reported.

Sheinbaum weighs in

President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Tuesday that the Federal Attorney General’s Office could assist UNAM in its investigation if required.

“They have to see how this fraud was committed,” she said.

It has to be established whether “the company … [UNAM] hired” to facilitate the online exams was complicit or whether “some” of the exam candidates used AI of their own accord, Sheinbaum said.

With reports from BBC, El País and Infobae

World.title: A 1.5-tonne sandwich sets a new world record at Mexico City’s Torta Fair
World.content:
A 100-meter torta weighing more than one and a half metric tons set a Guinness World Record in Mexico City on Wednesday at the capital’s annual Torta Fair.

Guinness World Records adjudicator Alfredo Arista certified the sandwich on the esplanade of the Venustiano Carranza borough, declaring to organizers, “From today you are officially amazing. Congratulations!”

Guinness declared the record to be in the category “the largest serving of sandwiches arranged in a continuous line” — with media and local officials describing it as the largest torta the world has ever seen.

Laid out on long rows of tables, the torta was then cut into segments and moved to industrial scales in a weighing process carried out under strict hygiene protocols and Guinness supervision.

Officials said the mega-torta measured 100 meters (about 328 feet) and tipped the scales at 1,570 kilograms (about 3,460 pounds). A metric ton, or tonne, is 1,000 kilograms.

The 2026 torta surpassed previous giant tortas assembled at the same festival, which reached 76 meters in 2024 and 90 meters in 2025 but did not carry Guinness certification.

The record-shattering event was documented by the Washington Post, the BBC, Reuters and other outlets.

Dozens of cooks, wearing caps, masks and gloves, assembled more than 50 varieties of fillings into a single continuous torta, including ham, breaded pork cutlet, sausage, beans, chistorra, mole, seafood, carnitas and even wild boar.

A torta in Mexican Spanish is a sandwich made on a roll, typically a bolillo or telera.

Once the weighing was complete, the sandwich was divided and distributed for free among the thousands of attendees.

Last year, volunteers in Toluca, the capital of México state, set what a notary public called a world record with an 82-meter chorizo torta. But that was specifically for a chorizo torta, nor was the record certified by Guinness.

For years, Guinness has turned down torta-specific records as part of their broader policy of avoiding overly specialized food categories.

While this week’s mega-torta did enter the record book, it did not break the Guinness marks for the world’s largest sandwich (2,467 kilograms, assembled in Michigan, 2005) or the world’s longest sandwich (735 meters, assembled in Lebanon, 2011).

The current five-day Torta Fair opened Wednesday and runs through Sunday. It includes more than 100 vendors offering torta styles from Mexican states such as Jalisco, Puebla and Yucatán, alongside international options from countries including Colombia, Spain and China.

Admission is free, and organizers expect more than 600,000 visitors and an economic impact above 50 million pesos (US $2.9 million), with concerts, cultural activities and a pet “Adoptathon” rounding out the program.

Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada noted there are roughly 10,000 torta businesses in the capital, calling the fair a showcase for local commerce and a celebration of the city’s everyday cuisine.

With reports from El Heraldo de Puebla, AFN, SDP Noticias and Reuters

World.title: World Cup spending fuels Mexico’s second-quarter economic rebound
World.content:
The Mexican economy grew 1.5% in the second quarter of 2026 compared to the previous three-month period, according to preliminary data, recovering from a 0.6% contraction in the first quarter of the year.

The quarter-over-quarter growth rate, reported by the national statistics agency INEGI on Thursday, was the best result for the Mexican economy since the final quarter of 2020.

INEGI also reported that Mexico’s economy grew 2.1% annually in the second quarter of 2026, up from a 0.4% year-over-year expansion in the first quarter.

Both the quarter-over-quarter and annual growth rates came in above the median forecasts of economists surveyed by Reuters.

On social media, Banco Base’s director of economic analysis, Gabriela Siller, wrote that it is “estimated that approximately two-thirds of the quarter-over-quarter growth was due to the World Cup effect, with the remainder the result of a rebound effect following the contraction in the first quarter.”

She said that the quarter-over-quarter GDP “boost” mainly came from the secondary sector, driven by spending on construction in April and May ahead of the World Cup, as well as the tertiary sector due to greater retail and services expenditure “associated with the event.”

Similarly, Andrés Abadia, chief Latin America economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics, said that economic activity in Mexico in the second quarter “benefited from temporary supports, such as the boost the World Cup gave to tourism, retail trade and spending on entertainment.”

Mexico hosted 13 matches during this year’s FIFA men’s World Cup, 12 of which were played in June.

INEGI published preliminary data last week that showed that the Mexican economy grew 0.2% on a sequential basis in June and 1.7% annually.

All 3 sectors grew in Q2

INEGI’s latest data showed that the primary sector grew 3.3% in the second quarter compared to the previous three-month period and 7.3% on an annual basis.

The secondary sector expanded 1.6% on a quarter-over-quarter basis and 0.8% annually, while the tertiary sector grew 1.5% sequentially and 2.5% compared to the first quarter of 2025.

While the primary sector recorded the strongest growth, Siller pointed out that its contribution to GDP is not significant compared to the other two sectors.

“Although primary activities showed the greatest quarter-over-quarter growth, they represent very little of GDP,” she wrote on X on Thursday morning.

“Of the 1.5% quarter-over-quarter growth, primary activities contributed 0.12 percentage points, while secondary activities contributed 0.49 pp and tertiary activities 0.90 pp,” Siller wrote.

The outlook for the Mexican economy

Earlier this month, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) lowered its 2026 growth forecast for Mexico to 1.2% from a previous prediction of 1.6%. Finance Minister Édgar Amador responded by expressing confidence that the economy will outperform the IMF projection. Indeed, the Finance Ministry is forecasting annual growth of between 1.8% and 2.8% this year.

While President Claudia Sheinbaum has predicted that economic activity will pick up in the second half of 2026 as new public and private investment projects commence, Siller anticipates a sequential contraction in the third quarter of the year.

The Banco Base analyst wrote on X that after the World Cup — Mexico hosted its final match on July 5 — “a downward correction in Mexico’s GDP is expected.”

“In other words, another [quarter-over-quarter] contraction,” Siller explained.

“This is because GDP measures the flow of goods and services produced in the country during a period, and production in the quarter following the World Cup will likely be lower in terms of construction, retail trade, and services, particularly services associated with the tourism sector and leisure activities.”

Una vez pasado el Mundial, se espera una corrección a la baja en el PIB de México, es decir, otra contracción. Esto se debe a que el PIB mide el flujo de los bienes y servicios que se producen en el país durante un periodo, y la producción en el trimestre posterior al Mundial… pic.twitter.com/29gR6A6YNG — Gabriela Siller Pagaza (@GabySillerP) July 30, 2026

In her post, Siller included a table showing pessimistic, central and optimistic forecasts for the third and fourth quarters, and 2026 as a whole. Her pessimistic forecast is that the Mexican economy will contract 1.2% on a sequential basis in the third quarter.

Abadia, the Pantheon Macroeconomics economist, asserted that the pace of growth recorded in the second quarter “won’t be sustainable,” while Goldman Sachs’ head of Latin American economics, Alberto Ramos, said that moving forward “it’s probable that [Mexican] households’ consumption of goods and services will continue facing obstacles derived from internal and external uncertainty and weak consumer confidence.”

With reports from El Economista and Reuters

World.title: Rain hampers cleanup of a hazardous chemical spill after a train derailment near the US border
World.content:
A weekend train derailment in Sonora resulted in the spillage of approximately 59,000 liters of sodium hydrosulfide, prompting the Federal Attorney General’s Office (FGR) to open an investigation.

The sodium hydrosulfide — a corrosive chemical compound used in industrial processes such as copper mining and considered hazardous to health and environment — was spilled after the derailment of several tank cars of a freight train belonging to Ferromex, a subsidiary of Grupo México.

Grupo México is one of the biggest copper producers in the world and Ferromex is the largest train network in Mexico.

Weekend rains complicated containment efforts, heightening concerns about the environmental impact of the accident in northern Sonora, about 20 kilometers south of the U.S. border.

Governor Alfonso Durazo told the newspaper La Jornada that the impact of the tank car hitting the ground partly contained the leak, noting that not all of the chemical seeped out. He added that the spill was immediately addressed by emergency services.

“We immediately focused on addressing the incident; emergency measures were implemented to remove any material that could pose a risk,” Daniel Gámez, the coordinator of Sonora’s Civil Protection Agency, said.

Gámez said the Federal Attorney for Environmental Protection (Profepa), the Environment Ministry and the FGR were notified immediately and emergency personnel established a security perimeter while continuing to evaluate the conditions at the site of the derailment.

Officials from the border-straddling community of Naco, 18 miles north of the accident site, said that rains on Sunday hampered the clean-up effort, allowing some of the spilled material to be carried away by natural runoff.

Lorenzo Villegas, mayor of the municipality of Naco on the Sonora side, told La Jornada that the smell of the fumes generated by the reaction of sodium hydrosulfide with water forced several families from the nearby Cuauhtémoc ejido to temporarily abandon their homes.

The National Water Commission is sampling water and soil to determine if the compound caused contamination.

Profepa is monitoring the situation due to the possibility that the chemical could reach waterways leading to Cananea, a city of approximately 40,000 about 10 miles further south.

With reports from La Silla Rota, Aristegui Noticias and La Jornada

World.title: US resumes cattle imports from Mexico, with plans to reduce screwworm danger
World.content:
The U.S. government will resume importing Mexican cattle next month, more than a year after the May 2025 suspension due at the time to “the continued and rapid northward spread of New World Screwworm (NWS) in Mexico.”

President Claudia Sheinbaum said the reopening of commerce will begin during the last weeks of August through the Mexican border port of Agua Prieta, Sonora.

🇺🇸 The New World screwworm was eradicated from America in 1966. In 2026, it tried to come back — and we were ready. That’s why USDA acted before it reached our border—investing over $1 billion, ramping up sterile fly production, and preparing an aggressive response. Just 60… pic.twitter.com/2St7SV1w4B — Secretary Brooke Rollins (@SecRollins) July 28, 2026

Sheinbaum expressed “great pleasure” to inform the public and especially ranchers of the U.S. decision. “This is great news for Mexican ranchers,” she said in a July 24 social media post. “I recognize the effort they have made for many months to contain the NWS plague.”

Mexico is required to enforce strict internal movement controls and documentary proof of treatment.

In a statement, U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins and the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) announced “a coordinated, phased reopening of southern cattle ports,” while explaining that the action was contingent on Mexico’s adherence to a Joint Action Plan.

The USDA acknowledged that Mexico’s northern border states of Sonora and Chihuahua “have maintained a strong animal health infrastructure program, built on the backs of successful animal disease control measures.”

As Sonora and Chihuahua are the lowest-risk states for the screwworm parasite, the reopening procedures will initially be limited to crossings in these two states.

Beginning Aug. 24, the USDA will allow cattle trade through the Douglas, Arizona, port of entry, while simultaneously taking the steps necessary for subsequent openings at two ports in New Mexico (Santa Teresa and Columbus) and their sister ports on the Mexican side (San Jerónimo, Chihuahua, and Puerto Palomas, Chihuahua, respectively).

Sheinbaum described the successful efforts to reopen the cattle trade as “a new example that dialogue, cooperation, and collaboration with mutual respect between Mexico and the United States yield great results for the benefit of our peoples.”

She thanked Secretary Rollins for her willingness to strengthen bilateral collaboration on health and trade matters, while also singling out Mexico’s Agriculture Ministry, Agriculture Minister Columba López and former Minister Julio Berdegué for praise. López succeeded Berdegué on May 1 of this year.

The easing of cattle crossings is expected to help the U.S. offset low herd counts that in January hit a 75-year low, as well as provide economic relief for ranchers, restore export revenue for Mexico and renew supply chain stability.

With reports from LopezDoriga.com, El Financiero and MarketWatch

World.title: Mexico in Numbers: Internet use hits record high, but rural gap persists
World.content:
What percentage of Mexicans are internet users?

How do internet connectivity rates differ across Mexico?

How many Mexican homes have computers?

Find out the answers to those questions in this week’s “Mexico in Numbers” article, which primarily focuses on internet use in Mexico.

* All of the data in this article comes from the results report of the latest National Survey on the Availability and Use of Information Technology in Homes (ENDUTIH). The survey was conducted by the national statistics agency INEGI in more than 65,000 homes between Aug. 25 and Oct. 17, 2025. INEGI published the results report in June 2026.

More than 8 in 10 Mexicans use the internet

Some 104.9 million people in Mexico were internet users in 2025, a figure equivalent to 86.1% of the population aged six and above.

The percentage of the population that uses the internet has gradually increased over the past decade. In 2022, the figure was 78.6% while in 2023 it was 81.2%.

In 2024, 83.1% of Mexicans aged 6 and older were internet users, a figure three percentage points below the most recent number.

Compared to 2015, the percentage of the Mexican population that were internet users in 2025 was 28.7 points higher.

The percentage of males aged six and older who use the internet was 86.6% last year, exactly one point higher than the figure for females (85.6%).

The urban/rural divide

INEGI reported that 88.9% of people who live in urban areas of Mexico were internet users in 2025. The figure for people who live in rural areas of the country was 75.2%.

Thus, the urban/rural internet use gap was 13.7 points in 2025, down from 27 points five years earlier.

Between 2020 and 2025, the percentage of urban internet users increased 10.7 points from 78.2% in the former year to 88.9% in the latter.

In the same period, the percentage of rural internet users increased 24 points, rising from 51.2% in 2020 to 75.2% last year.

The previous federal government launched a “Social Coverage Program” to increase internet coverage in rural parts of Mexico.

Nuevo León has the highest percentage of internet users

In 2025, 93.9% of residents of the northern state of Nuevo León were internet users, the highest rate among Mexico’s 32 federal entities.

Baja California ranked second (93.2%), followed by Quintana Roo (92.1%).

More than 90% of the populations of four other entities were internet users in 2025: Baja California Sur, Nayarit, Aguascalientes and Mexico City.

The southern state of Chiapas had the lowest percentage of internet users in 2025. Just 71.2% of Chiapanecos were internet users last year. The only other state with a rate lower than 80% was Oaxaca (78.6%).

Teens and young adults are the most connected cohort

In 2025, the percentage of internet users in eight different age cohorts was as follows:

6-14: 85.4%

15-24: 97.6%

25-34: 96.5%

35-44: 94.3%

45-54: 88.9%

55-64: 78.8%

65-74: 57.8%

75+: 30.3%

While the percentage of internet users aged 75 and over was low, it was much higher in 2025 than in 2015, when just 3% of that age cohort went online.

More than 8 in 10 Mexicans have cell phones

In 2025, there were 103.2 million cell phone users in Mexico, representing 84.6% of the population aged six and over. That percentage increased 13.2 points from 71.4% in 2015.

The vast majority of cell phone users in Mexico — 97% — use smartphones.

Among those people, 90.6% use instant messaging apps such as WhatsApp on their phones, while 80.4% access social media.

Almost eight in 10 (77.8%) smartphone users access audio and video content on their devices, while 52% make use of navigation apps such as Google Maps and Waze.

The percentage of Mexican homes with computers has declined over the past decade

In 2025, some 17.7 million Mexican homes — 44.7% of all homes in the country — had a computer, be it a desktop, a laptop or a tablet.

The percentage rose 0.8 points compared to 2024, but declined 0.2 points compared to 2015, when 44.9% of Mexican homes had a computer. The decline over the past decade is indicative of the rise of the smartphone, which in many ways is a small computer.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: Arturo Estrada, the last surviving student of Frida Kahlo, turns 101 today
World.content:
If there’s someone who’s been able to depict the colors of Mexico, it is Arturo Estrada, a student of Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera who turns 101 years old today. This is his story.

The dreamscapes of Arturo Estrada

Arturo Estrada’s painting has fascinated diverse audiences. Its fluidity, forcefulness and color turn his works into windows from which to look out into a dream. His figures metamorphose; his canvases dance to the melody of life. Fruits are people, people are trees; a flower is a star, a bird and a stone.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Mtro. Arturo Estrada (@frido.arturoestrada)

Estrada allows himself to be captivated by the natural world. He permits his mind to transform it, delivering it — lovingly crafted — to our eyes and hearts.

His origins

Arturo Estrada Hernández was born in 1925 in Panindícuaro, a town nestled in the mountains of Michoacán. The artist claims to have known his vocation from the very first moment: to be a painter. This journey began with his observations of the countryside, the clouds and the animals. He watched leather transform into footwear in the family shoe shop and, above all, flipped through books and newspapers, copying photographs and illustrations he found within their pages.

Part of his education took place during the Cristero War, when Catholic worship was forced underground. While still a child, he became an apprentice to the religious sculptor Miguel Moreno, from whom he learned the craft of carving religious effigies in wood and received his first painting lessons. Some of his early works were altarpieces and biblical scenes. At age 15, already with an established path in art, he moved to Mexico City to study formally.

La Esmeralda

Arturo Estrada entered the School of Painting and Sculpture of the Ministry of Public Education, known as La Esmeralda. The institution, which had a notable social mission, was dedicated to training artists and provided them with all the necessary tools. Meaning, in addition to being free, it covered the cost of materials and offered scholarships and other incentives.

In 1943, painter Antonio Ruiz, nicknamed “El Corcito,” became the director of La Esmeralda and invited his friends — artists of great renown — to teach at the school. This was how Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera came to head the courses in Pictorial Initiation and Mural Painting, respectively. Estrada enrolled in both courses, where he developed a close friendship with the couple, one that would leave a lasting mark on his life and his painting.

‘Los Fridos’

Amusing and dedicated, Frida Kahlo was an unusual teacher who quickly won the affection of her students. When her health declined, the group followed her to the garden of the Casa Azul (the Blue House). There, they established a painting workshop, led by their mentor.

Alongside Kahlo’s other students, Arturo Estrada painted his first mural at the pulquería La Rosita in Coyoacán. Commuting to that town from Mexico City was not easy, so the number of students dwindled until only the four known as “Los Fridos” remained. Along with Fanny Rabel, Arturo García Bustos and Guillermo Monroy, Arturo Estrada was a staple presence at Casa Azul for more than 10 years.

Kahlo and Rivera’s disciples painted murals in the auditorium of the Casa de la Madre Soltera and in the banquet hall of the Hotel Posada del Sol (this time featuring only the work of Estrada, Monroy and García Bustos).

Estrada as a teacher and emerging artist

Arturo Estrada balanced his creative career with teaching at La Esmeralda for more than four decades. He started as a professor shortly after graduating, and over the years he taught classes in oil and tempera, figure drawing and mural painting. In 1983, he was named director of the school, a position he used to elevate its educational offerings to a bachelor’s degree level.

From very early on, his solo work was widely celebrated, a recognition that opened valuable doors for him both at home and abroad. His experience as an assistant on murals by José Clemente Orozco, Juan O’Gorman and Diego Rivera qualified him to take on major artistic challenges.

For the SCOP Center, he designed the stone mosaic “El Aire” (“The Air”). He also received commissions for the mural “Tríptico de la Independencia” (“Independence Triptych”) in Cuautla, Morelos, and the decoration of the Nuevo Laredo Water Treatment Plant, crafted in Italian mosaic.

After participating in numerous collective exhibitions, he presented his first solo show in 1955 at the Salón de la Plástica Mexicana. The centerpiece of the exhibition was the painting “Vida-Muerte de Frida Kahlo” (“Life-Death of Frida Kahlo”), which he had painted from a sketch made at his teacher’s funeral. Both Diego Rivera and Juan O’Gorman published positive reviews of the exhibition, which was also praised by Miguel Covarrubias and Doctor Atl.

Establishing a reputation for quality

In 1957, Marcel Duchamp visited the studio that Estrada shared with other artists in Mexico City. Following this encounter, the Frenchman supported the Michoacán native’s candidacy for the William and Noma Copley Foundation fellowship, for which he served as a juror.

Thanks to this support, Estrada traveled to Europe, where he immersed himself in Renaissance art and the avant-garde, and spent time with fellow fellowship winners such as Max Ernst and Roberto Matta. The following year, he was invited to various cities in East Germany and the Soviet Union, traveling from Russia to Armenia on a study and networking trip.

During the 1960s, he was called upon to paint murals at the Casa de la Juventud in San Luis Potosí, the Capilla Morelos in Nocupétaro and the National Museum of Anthropology, where he depicted the festivities of the Virgin of Juquila, Oaxaca, in the work “Pedimento o Manda” (“Petition or Vow”). He also painted several works for the church of San Andrés in his native Panindícuaro.

In 1988, Estrada created “Medicina Tradicional y Medicina Contemporánea” (“Traditional Medicine and Contemporary Medicine”). Located at the Centro Médico station of the Mexico City Metro, this mural is viewed daily by thousands of people.

Arturo Estrada today

At 101 years old, Arturo Estrada experiences art with a profound love. Recent exhibitions of his work have drawn crowds who never cease to marvel at his ingenuity. In 2024, he received the Gold Fine Arts Medal (Medalla Bellas Artes de Oro), awarded by the government to the most notable figures in Mexican creation. Humble, passionate and playful, the painter still enjoys life with an enthusiasm that shines through each of his brushstrokes.

Lydia Leija is a linguist, journalist and visual storyteller. She has directed three feature films, and her audiovisual work has been featured in national and international media. She’s been part of National Geographic, Muy Interesante and Cosmopolitan.

World.title: Neymar Museum Opens at Brazil’s Santos FC Stadium
World.content:
Sports · Brazil

Key Facts —Location The Neymar gallery is inside the Memorial das Conquistas museum at Santos FC’s Vila Belmiro stadium in Santos, São Paulo state. —Exclusive Honor Neymar and Pelé are the only two players with individual, dedicated galleries in the club’s official museum. —Artifacts The exhibition displays a bronze bust, a full statue, and an autographed blue Santos number 10 jersey worn by Neymar. —Titles Listed The bust’s base lists Neymar’s Santos trophies: three Paulista championships (2010-2012), the 2010 Copa do Brasil, and the 2011 Copa Libertadores. —Ceremony Neymar attended the July 30, 2026 inauguration and described the personal gallery as ‘an honour’.

Santos Futebol Clube has inaugurated a permanent Neymar museum wing inside its stadium, making the active Brazilian forward only the second player in the club’s history to receive a dedicated personal gallery. The tribute, opened on July 30, 2026, places Neymar alongside the legendary Pelé in the Memorial das Conquistas at the historic Vila Belmiro.

Neymar in Santos colours. The club has opened a dedicated gallery in his honour at Vila Belmiro. (Photo internet reproduction)

Inside the New Neymar Museum Wing

The newly designed space features a bronze bust of Neymar, a full statue, and an autographed blue Santos number 10 jersey on display. The bust’s base is engraved with the major titles he won during his first spell with the club.

Those achievements include three consecutive São Paulo state championships, known as the Campeonato Paulista, from 2010 through 2012. The engraving also lists the 2010 Copa do Brasil and the 2011 Copa Libertadores, South America’s most prestigious club competition.

A Tribute Reserved for Royalty

Santos FC formally designated Neymar as the ‘Príncipe da Vila,’ which translates to the Prince of the Village. The title directly positions him as the modern heir to Pelé, who is eternally known as ‘O Rei,’ or The King.

Before this inauguration, Pelé stood alone as the only individual player with a personal gallery inside the Memorial das Conquistas. The club’s decision to build a second dedicated wing highlights Neymar’s unique status in its 112-year history.

The Significance of Vila Belmiro

For an international audience, understanding the venue is essential. The Memorial das Conquistas is located inside Vila Belmiro, the club’s compact and fiercely atmospheric stadium in the port city of Santos, São Paulo state.

Vila Belmiro is hallowed ground in football history because it served as Pelé’s primary stage for nearly his entire professional career. Housing Neymar’s permanent tribute inside this same building physically links the two eras for visiting expats, investors, and tourists.

Neymar’s Journey Back to His Roots

Neymar attended the July 30 ceremony and told assembled media that receiving a personal gallery was ‘an honour.’ His presence highlighted a career that has come full circle after he emerged from the club’s famed youth academy as a teenager.

He left Santos in 2013 to play for FC Barcelona, later moving to Paris Saint-Germain and Al-Hilal. In 2025, he completed a high-profile return to his boyhood club, reigniting local pride and global interest in the team.

The museum wing celebrates not just the trophies from his early years but also the enduring bond between the player and the institution that launched him. It solidifies his legacy while he is still an active contributor on the pitch.

What Visitors Can Expect

International visitors to the Memorial das Conquistas can now walk through two distinct player galleries. The Pelé exhibit remains a comprehensive archive of the king’s global impact, featuring historic boots, balls, and iconic jerseys.

The Neymar wing offers a modern counterpoint, centered on the bronze bust and statue that capture the star in his prime. The display is designed to be a pilgrimage site for a new generation of global fans traveling to Brazil.

The museum is open to the public on matchdays and through scheduled tours, providing a direct look at how a traditional Brazilian club honors its living legends. No local currency figures were disclosed for the construction of the exhibit.

A Legacy Set in Bronze

By immortalizing Neymar in bronze while he is still playing, Santos FC breaks with the convention of reserving statues solely for retired icons. The move reflects his role in winning the club’s first Copa Libertadores title since the Pelé era in 1963.

The dual galleries now bookend the story of Santos FC for foreign observers: the mid-20th century dynasty of Pelé and the 21st-century resurgence led by Neymar. The museum transforms individual achievement into a tangible narrative of continuity.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where is the Neymar museum located?

The Neymar gallery is located inside the Memorial das Conquistas, the official museum of Santos FC, which is situated within the Vila Belmiro stadium in Santos, São Paulo, Brazil.

Is Neymar the only player with a museum wing at Santos?

No. Neymar is the second player to receive a dedicated personal gallery. The only other individual with a dedicated wing is Pelé, widely regarded as one of the greatest footballers of all time.

What items are displayed in the Neymar museum wing?

The exhibition features a bronze bust of Neymar, a full statue, and an autographed blue Santos number 10 jersey. The base of the bust lists his major title wins with the club.

World.title: Haiti Elections Set for 2026 Amid Gang Rule in Capital
World.content:
Caribbean · Haiti

Key Facts —Election date First-round presidential and legislative elections are scheduled for December 13, 2026. —Runoff and local vote A runoff election and municipal vote are planned for February 21, 2027. —Referendum A constitutional referendum will be held on the same day as the first round, December 13, 2026. —Political parties A record 280 political parties registered to participate in the elections. —Security context The vote is contingent on improved security; gangs control much of the capital, Port-au-Prince.

Haiti elections are now scheduled for December 13, 2026, marking the first general vote in a decade for the Caribbean nation of 11.7 million people. The Provisional Electoral Council, known as the CEP, released the revised calendar setting a first round of presidential and legislative contests alongside a constitutional referendum.

Haiti Elections Set for December 2026 After Decade-Long Wait. (Photo internet reproduction)

The Revised Electoral Timeline

The CEP’s calendar sets the first round for December 13, 2026. This date combines presidential, legislative, and a constitutional referendum into a single voting day.

If no presidential candidate wins outright, a runoff will follow on February 21, 2027. Local and municipal elections will also take place on that date.

Final results are expected to be published around March 7, 2027. The original plan had called for elections on August 30, 2026.

That earlier timetable was postponed because of severe gang violence and deep security fears across the country. Officials pushed the date back by four months to allow more preparation time.

A Record Field of Political Parties

A record 280 political parties registered by the deadline to take part in the process. This is an unusually high number for any national election.

The vast field reflects a fragmented political landscape. Haiti has lacked elected officials since early 2023, creating a vacuum that many groups now seek to fill.

The last general elections were held in 2016. Since then, the political system has unraveled, especially after the assassination of President Jovenel Moïse in July 2021.

Currently, a Transitional Presidential Council, or CPT, governs the country. It was formed to guide Haiti toward a return to democratic order.

Haiti elections and the Security Challenge

The entire electoral process remains contingent on improved security. Widespread gang violence continues to control large swaths of the capital, Port-au-Prince.

Armed groups have strangled key transport routes and neighborhoods. Their influence raises serious doubts about whether a free and fair vote can physically take place.

A Kenya-led Multinational Security Support mission, known as the MSS, has been deployed to assist the Haitian National Police. The mission aims to reclaim territory from gangs.

Despite this international support, security conditions remain fragile. Many observers question whether the December timeline is realistic without a major shift in the security landscape.

Funding and Logistical Hurdles

Organizing a nationwide vote in Haiti is a massive and expensive undertaking. The CEP must register voters, print ballots, and secure thousands of polling stations.

Funding for the elections is not yet fully secured. International donors have often shouldered the cost of Haitian elections, but commitments remain unclear for this cycle.

Logistical challenges are compounded by the country’s deep poverty. Haiti is the poorest nation in the Western Hemisphere, with infrastructure crippled by years of crisis.

Delivering materials to remote areas and ensuring the safety of election workers will test the capacity of the state and its international partners.

What the Referendum Means

Voters will also decide on a new constitution on December 13. The current document has been a source of political conflict for years.

Details of the proposed changes have not been widely publicized. The referendum was a key demand of some political factions before holding elections.

Holding the referendum and the first-round vote on the same day is a high-risk gamble. It doubles the complexity for electoral authorities and could confuse voters.

For international observers, the combined vote raises concerns about transparency. The success of the entire process hinges on the CEP’s ability to manage both contests simultaneously.

International Context and Outlook

Foreign governments, including the United States, have pushed for elections as a path to stability. They view a legitimate government as essential for long-term recovery.

However, the international community remains cautious. The MSS mission is under-resourced, and previous international interventions in Haiti have a troubled legacy.

The record number of parties could also lead to a highly fragmented legislature. This might make governing difficult even if the elections are held successfully.

For now, the December 13 date is a target, not a guarantee. The coming months will test whether Haiti can overcome its security and funding crises to hold a credible vote.

Frequently Asked Questions

When are the Haiti elections scheduled?

The first round of presidential and legislative elections is scheduled for December 13, 2026. A runoff and local elections are planned for February 21, 2027.

Why were the Haiti elections postponed?

The elections were originally planned for August 2026 but were postponed due to widespread gang violence and severe security fears, particularly in the capital, Port-au-Prince.

How many political parties are running in the Haiti elections?

A record 280 political parties registered to participate, reflecting a deeply fragmented political landscape after years without elected officials.

World.title: Botero Dove of Peace Removed from Colombia’s Presidential Palace
World.content:
Culture · Colombia

Key Facts —Sculpture Fernando Botero’s bronze ‘La Paloma de la Paz’ (Dove of Peace) was removed from the presidential palace in Bogotá. —Timing The move is part of the routine presidential transition ahead of Abelardo De La Espriella’s August 7, 2026 inauguration. —Donation Botero donated the work on September 24, 2016, just before the government signed a historic peace accord with the FARC guerrillas. —Location The sculpture has been returned to the National Museum in Bogotá, where it was previously housed. —Protocol Moving symbolic art pieces during transitions is standard practice; the same protocol was followed when Juan Manuel Santos left office.

Colombia has removed the Botero Dove of Peace from the presidential palace and returned it to the National Museum, officials confirmed, marking a symbolic shift ahead of the August 7 presidential transition.

Colombia Returns Botero Dove of Peace Ahead of Transition. (Photo internet reproduction)
